# Developer portals from OpenAPI

> Turn OpenAPI specs and Markdown guides into a developer portal. Docs as code, static output, optional single sign-on (SSO).

## What you get

**[Interactive API reference](/docs/api-reference/reference-pages/)**

Every OpenAPI 3.0, 3.1 or Swagger 2.0 spec gets a reference page rendered by RapiDoc, with Try, code samples and a sidebar that stays in view.

**[Guides as code](/docs/writing/markdown/)**

Markdown, MDX and Markdoc pages in a `docs/` folder. Callouts, tabs, steps, cards, and live API operations inside a guide.

**[One config file](/docs/configuration/overview/)**

`rapidoc.config.yaml` describes the header, tabs, sidebars, theme and footer. An unknown key fails the build with its path and a hint.

**[Search built in](/docs/configuration/docs-search-redirects/)**

Full-text search across guides and API operations, indexed at build time. No search service to run.

**[Single sign-on (SSO)](/docs/access/overview/)**

Optional SSO with Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google or any OpenID Connect provider. Decide who may read which pages, APIs and files, by group or email.

**[Mock server](/docs/tools/mock-server/)**

Serve your specs with their examples, validate requests, and check OAuth tokens and scopes, so you can use Try before your API is deployed.

## From zero to portal

```bash
npm create rapidoc@latest my-portal
cd my-portal
npm install
npm run dev
```

The starter is a portal with an example API, a `rapidoc.config.yaml` and two guides, running on `http://localhost:4321`. Then point it at your own spec. Already have a repository with OpenAPI files? Run `npx @rapidoc/cli init` there instead. [Read the quickstart](/docs/getting-started/quickstart/).

## A live operation, right in a guide

Guides can embed any operation from your specs. This one comes from the [example Bookstore API](/apis/bookstore/). Its **Try** button sends a real request: run the [mock server](/docs/tools/mock-server/) to get answers before your API exists.

`GET /books` ([Bookstore API](/apis/bookstore))

> **Note: Moving from Zudoku or Redocly?**
> `npx @rapidoc/cli migrate` writes a `rapidoc.config.yaml` from your existing Zudoku or Redocly project. [See migrating](/docs/tools/migrate/).

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/

---

# Introduction

> What RapiDoc Portal is, what it builds, and which package does what.

RapiDoc Portal is a docs-as-code developer portal framework. You keep your OpenAPI specs and your guides in a repository, describe the site in one `rapidoc.config.yaml`, and the `rapidoc` command builds a static portal from them.

A portal has:

- **A home page** from `docs/index.md`, `.mdx` or `.markdoc`.
- **Guides** under `/docs/...`, written in Markdown, MDX or [Markdoc](https://markdoc.dev) (Markdown with tags, made by Stripe).
- **An interactive API reference** for each spec at `/apis/<id>`, rendered by the [RapiDoc](https://rapidocui.com) web component. Each operation has a **Try** button that sends a real request to your API from the browser.
- **An API catalog** at `/catalog`, with every API grouped by category.
- **Full-text search** across guides and API operations.
- **A header with tabs.** A documentation tab has its own sidebar of guides; an API tab opens an API's reference.
- **A footer, a banner, and light and dark themes**, styled with your brand ([Customizing the portal](/docs/configuration/customizing/)).

And, when you need them:

- **API versions**, each with its own URLs and a version picker ([Versions](/docs/api-reference/versions/)).
- **Arazzo workflows**: multi-step API journeys, in the OpenAPI Initiative's Arazzo format, drawn as diagrams you can run step by step ([Workflows](/docs/configuration/workflows/)).
- **Single sign-on (SSO) and access rules**: Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google or any OpenID Connect provider, with pages and APIs per group ([Single sign-on (SSO)](/docs/access/overview/)). **Try** can call your API with the reader's own token.
- **A mock server** that answers from your specs' examples and checks OAuth tokens and scopes, so you can use Try before your API is deployed ([Mock server](/docs/tools/mock-server/)).
- **MCP tools for AI agents** (Model Context Protocol): your APIs and workflows as tools, exported or hosted at `/mcp` under the same access rules ([MCP server](/docs/tools/mcp-server/)).
- **`llms.txt`**, an index of the site for AI assistants, and **Markdown copies** of every page ([LLM output](/docs/configuration/llms/)).
- **Spec checks in CI**: [validate](/docs/tools/validate/), [lint](/docs/tools/lint/) and [bundle](/docs/tools/bundle/) your OpenAPI files.
- **Migration** from Zudoku or Redocly with one command ([Migrate](/docs/tools/migrate/)).

The output is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Host it on GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel, Cloudflare Pages, S3 or any web server ([Static hosting](/docs/deploy/static-hosting/)).

## The packages

| Package | What it does |
| :--- | :--- |
| `@rapidoc/cli` | The `rapidoc` command you run, directly or through the `npm run` scripts: `init`, `dev`, `build`, `serve`, `mock`, `validate`, `lint`, `migrate` and [more](/docs/reference/cli/). |
| `@rapidoc/portal` | The engine behind `rapidoc dev` and `rapidoc build`: config, layout, Markdoc tags, search. |
| `@rapidoc/server` | Behind `rapidoc serve`: serves a built portal with single sign-on (OpenID Connect) and access rules. Optional. |
| `@rapidoc/mock` | Behind `rapidoc mock`: a mock server for the portal's APIs, with request validation and token checks. Optional. |
| `create-rapidoc` | `npm create rapidoc` scaffolds a new portal project. |
| `rapidoc` | The `<rapi-doc>` web component that renders each API reference. |

The CLI loads `@rapidoc/portal`, `@rapidoc/server` and `@rapidoc/mock` only for the commands that need them. `rapidoc init` and `rapidoc validate <spec>` work without `@rapidoc/portal` installed: run them as `npx @rapidoc/cli init` before anything is installed.

## Why another portal framework?

- **Docs as code.** Everything is a file in your repository: review it in pull requests, build it in CI.
- **Static by default.** No database and no runtime to operate. Per-page sign-in is the one feature that needs a server, and it's opt-in. A portal that is private as a whole can sit behind your SSO proxy as static files ([Static hosting](/docs/deploy/static-hosting/#need-sign-in-sso)).
- **Strict config.** An unknown key fails the build with its path and a hint, so a typo never disappears silently.
- **Accessible.** The layout is tested against WCAG 2.1 AA in both themes and at phone width, and accent text colors are derived from your brand color so they keep 4.5:1 contrast.

Next: [build your first portal](/docs/getting-started/quickstart/).

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/getting-started/introduction/

---

# Quickstart

> Create a portal, see it running, add your own OpenAPI spec, and build it for production.

In a few minutes you'll have a portal running on your computer with an example API, then with your own spec, and a static build ready to upload.

## Prerequisites

- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 22.12 or later. Check with `node --version`.
- Your OpenAPI 3.0, 3.1 or Swagger 2.0 file, if you have one. The starter includes an example, so you can add yours later.

Already have a repository with OpenAPI files? Skip to [Add a portal to an existing repository](#add-a-portal-to-an-existing-repository).

## Create a portal

**Create the project**

```bash
npm create rapidoc@latest my-portal
```

It asks for the site title (press Enter to keep "My Portal") and creates the folder `my-portal` with the [starter files](#what-the-starter-contains). It doesn't install anything yet.

**Install the dependencies**

```bash
cd my-portal
npm install
```

This installs the `rapidoc` command and the portal engine into `node_modules/`. It takes a minute or two.

**Start the dev server**

```bash
npm run dev
```

Open `http://localhost:4321` in your browser (or run `npm run dev -- --open`). You should see:

- the home page with your site title,
- the example API under the **Core API** tab (`/apis/core/`), with a **Try** button on each operation that sends a real request,
- two starter guides under the **Documentation** tab.

Leave the server running. A change to a guide in `docs/` shows up as soon as you save; a change to `rapidoc.config.yaml` or a spec restarts the server.

**Add your own spec**

Copy your OpenAPI file into `specs/`, then point the example API at it in `rapidoc.config.yaml`:

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
apis:
  - id: core
    spec: ./specs/orders.yaml   # your file
```

Reload `/apis/core/`: it now shows your API. The tab is still called **Core API**: change its `label` under `navigation:`. The `id` is the page's address (`/apis/<id>`); to rename it, also change `api: core` under `navigation:` and the `/apis/core` link under `header:`.

The starter guide `docs/guides/overview.markdoc` embeds the example's `GET /items` operation. Change it to one of your operations, or delete it. To add more APIs, add entries under `apis:` ([APIs](/docs/configuration/apis/)).

**Make it yours**

Change `site.title` in `rapidoc.config.yaml` and save: the header shows the new title once the server has restarted. The same file holds the logo, the theme color, the header links and the sidebar; guides are Markdown, MDX or Markdoc files in `docs/`. See [Configuration](/docs/configuration/overview/) and [Writing guides](/docs/writing/markdown/).

**Build for production**

Stop the dev server (Ctrl+C), then:

```bash
npm run build
```

The portal is written to `dist/` as plain static files: HTML pages, your specs and the search index. To look at the build before uploading it, run `npm run preview`. Then upload `dist/` to any static host: see [Static hosting](/docs/deploy/static-hosting/).

## Add a portal to an existing repository

In a repository that already has OpenAPI files, run this in its root folder:

```bash
npx @rapidoc/cli init
```

It finds the OpenAPI files, asks which ones to list in the portal, the site title, and whether to install the dependencies. Then it writes `rapidoc.config.yaml` and the [starter files](#what-the-starter-contains) next to your code. Each spec becomes an API whose id comes from its file name: `specs/orders-api.yaml` is `/apis/orders-api/`.

- **No `package.json` yet:** init creates one with the `dev`, `build` and `validate` scripts. Continue with `npm install` (if you didn't let init install) and `npm run dev`, as in steps 2 and 3 above.
- **A `package.json` already exists:** init keeps it and prints what to add. Install the CLI and the engine, then start the dev server:

  ```bash
  npm install -D @rapidoc/cli @rapidoc/portal
  npx rapidoc dev
  ```

init never overwrites a file that exists, unless you pass `--force`. Its other options, such as `--spec <file>`, `--title` and `--yes` (no questions), are in the [CLI reference](/docs/reference/cli/).

> **Note: npx rapidoc or npx @rapidoc/cli?**
> The command is `rapidoc`, from the npm package `@rapidoc/cli`. Before the CLI is installed in a project, run it as `npx @rapidoc/cli <command>`: `npx rapidoc` would look for the npm package `rapidoc`, which is the `<rapi-doc>` web component and has no command. Once `@rapidoc/cli` is installed, `npx rapidoc <command>` and the `npm run` scripts both work.

## What the starter contains

```text
my-portal/
├── rapidoc.config.yaml   # site, header, navigation, theme, APIs
├── package.json          # dev, build, start, validate and preview scripts
├── specs/api.yaml        # the example API (id: core)
├── docs/
│   ├── index.markdoc     # the home page
│   ├── getting-started.md
│   └── guides/overview.markdoc
├── render.yaml           # one-click deploy on Render (optional)
├── README.md
└── .gitignore            # node_modules/, dist/, .rapidoc-temp/, .env
```

What each folder is for: [Project structure](/docs/getting-started/project-structure/). `render.yaml` is only for [Render](/docs/deploy/cloud-platforms/); delete it if you deploy elsewhere.

## Troubleshooting

| What you see | What to do |
| :--- | :--- |
| `rapidoc: command not found` | Run `npm install` in the project folder first. |
| `npm error could not determine executable to run` | You ran `npx rapidoc` before the CLI was installed. Use `npx @rapidoc/cli` instead. |
| Port 4321 is in use | The dev server offers another port. To pick one yourself: `npm run dev -- --port 3000`. |
| The build stops on `rapidoc.config.yaml` | The error names the key and its path, and suggests the right key for a typo. See [Configuration](/docs/configuration/overview/). |
| Anything else | Run `npx rapidoc doctor`: it checks the Node version, the packages' versions and the config. |

## Next steps

- [Add more APIs](/docs/configuration/apis/), with categories and versions.
- [Write guides](/docs/writing/markdown/), with live operations from your APIs.
- [Set the theme, header and sidebar](/docs/configuration/overview/).
- Check your specs in CI with `npm run validate` ([Validate](/docs/tools/validate/)).
- [Deploy](/docs/deploy/static-hosting/) to any static host.
- [Put the portal behind single sign-on (SSO)](/docs/access/overview/), or only some of its pages and APIs.

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/getting-started/quickstart/
