# Project structure

> Where the config, specs, guides and static files go, and how files become URLs.

A portal is a folder with one config file and three folders. This is the starter from the [Quickstart](/docs/getting-started/quickstart/), plus a `public/` folder, which you create when you need one:

```text
my-portal/
├── rapidoc.config.yaml        # site, header, navigation, theme, APIs
├── package.json               # dev, build, start, validate and preview scripts
├── specs/                     # OpenAPI 3.0, 3.1 or Swagger 2.0 files, YAML or JSON
│   └── api.yaml
├── docs/                      # guides: .md, .mdx or .markdoc
│   ├── index.markdoc          # the home page (optional)
│   ├── getting-started.md
│   └── guides/
│       └── overview.markdoc
└── public/                    # optional: logo, favicon, images
```

## `rapidoc.config.yaml`

The one config file: the site, the header, the navigation, the theme and the APIs. See [Configuration](/docs/configuration/overview/).

## `docs/`

Every file is a page. The path decides the URL:

| File | URL |
| :--- | :--- |
| `docs/index.markdoc` | `/` (the home page) |
| `docs/getting-started.md` | `/docs/getting-started` |
| `docs/guides/overview.markdoc` | `/docs/guides/overview` |

In the config's `navigation:`, a page is named by its path without the extension, its *slug*: `guides/overview`. Without a `docs/index.*`, `/` redirects to the first tab.

Change the folder with `docs.dir` in the config. If both `page.md` and `page.mdx` exist, the `.mdx` one is used.

## `specs/`

OpenAPI files, listed under `apis:` in the config ([APIs](/docs/configuration/apis/)). Relative `$ref`s to other files resolve. A spec can also be a URL. Each API is published at `/specs/<api id>.<ext>`, so readers can download it.

## `public/`

Copied to the site root as-is: `public/logo.svg` is `/logo.svg`. Put the logo, favicon and images for guides here. Don't use it as the build's output folder.

## What a build leaves behind

Only the output folder, `dist/`. While it runs, a build works in a temporary folder, `.rapidoc-temp/`, inside the project, and removes it at the end, even when the build fails. Keep both out of Git, together with `.env`, where the [sign-in secrets](/docs/access/setup/#3-test-on-your-computer) go for local testing. The starter's `.gitignore` lists them:

```text
node_modules/
dist/
.rapidoc-temp/
.DS_Store
.env
.env.*
```

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/getting-started/project-structure/

---

# Configuration overview

> How rapidoc.config.yaml is organized, its conventions, and editor autocomplete.

Everything about the site lives in `rapidoc.config.yaml` at the project root. Only `site.title` is required, so the smallest config is:

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
site:
  title: Acme Developers
```

Every top-level key:

```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=./node_modules/@rapidoc/portal/schema.json
site:        # title, logo, favicon, URL, banner
theme:       # accent color, light/dark mode, fonts
head:        # extra tags in every page's <head> (analytics, fonts)
header:      # row 1: links and menus right of the search
navigation:  # row 2: one tab per entry; documentation tabs have a sidebar
apis:        # your OpenAPI specs
workflows:   # Arazzo workflow files
docs:        # docs folder, table of contents, edit links
footer:      # call to action, columns, social links, newsletter
rapidoc:     # <rapi-doc> attributes for API reference pages
search:      # full-text search on or off
llms:        # llms.txt and Markdown copies for AI assistants
redirects:   # old URLs to new ones
lint:        # rules for rapidoc lint
auth:        # single sign-on with OpenID Connect (optional)
access:      # who may read what (optional)
```

## Conventions

The same three words mean the same thing everywhere:

- `label` is the text of anything clickable.
- `href` is any URL: a path on this site (`/docs/intro`) or a full URL.
- `items` are children: dropdown items, mega-menu links, sidebar groups.

A navigation item's kind comes from its keys:

- `slug` (or a plain string): a page in `docs/`, by its path without the extension;
- `href`: a link;
- `items`: a group;
- `autogenerate`: every page in a folder of `docs/`;
- `api`: an API's reference page;
- `catalog`: the API catalog.

See [Navigation](/docs/configuration/navigation/).

## Strict by design

The schema rejects unknown keys. A typo fails the build with its path and, where it can, the key you meant:

```text
navigation[0].items[2]: unknown key "path" (use href (links) or slug (doc pages))
```

## Autocomplete in your editor

The starter's config already starts with this line. It points editors that understand YAML schemas (VS Code with the YAML extension, JetBrains IDEs) at the JSON Schema that ships as `@rapidoc/portal/schema.json`:

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
# yaml-language-server: $schema=./node_modules/@rapidoc/portal/schema.json
```

You get completion, descriptions on hover, and errors as you type.

## Other formats

The engine also reads `rapidoc.config.yml`, `.json`, `.js`, `.mjs` and `.ts`. A JavaScript or TypeScript config default-exports the same object.

## The sections

- [Site](/docs/configuration/site/): title, logo, favicon, URL, banner
- [Theme](/docs/configuration/theme/): accent color, mode, fonts
- [Header](/docs/configuration/header/): links, dropdowns, mega-menus
- [Navigation](/docs/configuration/navigation/): tabs and sidebars
- [APIs](/docs/configuration/apis/): specs, ids, categories
- [Workflows](/docs/configuration/workflows/): Arazzo files, drawn and runnable in the docs
- [Footer](/docs/configuration/footer/): call to action, columns, social links, newsletter
- [Docs, search and redirects](/docs/configuration/docs-search-redirects/): the docs folder, edit links, search, old URLs
- [LLM output](/docs/configuration/llms/): `llms.txt` and Markdown copies of every page
- [Single sign-on (SSO)](/docs/access/overview/): `auth` and `access`, for private pages and APIs

Every key in one table: [Configuration keys](/docs/reference/config/).

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/configuration/overview/

---

# Customizing the portal

> Every way to change how the portal looks and behaves - brand, layout, your own CSS, components in guides, API reference options and build scripts.

A portal looks like your product without forking the framework. Each layer below has its own page; this one shows what goes where.

## Brand and layout: `rapidoc.config.yaml`

| Change | Where |
| :--- | :--- |
| Accent color, light and dark mode, fonts | [Theme](/docs/configuration/theme/) |
| Logo (light and dark), favicon, link previews, announcement banner | [Site](/docs/configuration/site/) |
| Header links, buttons, dropdowns and mega-menus | [Header](/docs/configuration/header/) |
| Tabs and their sidebars, with icons and badges | [Navigation](/docs/configuration/navigation/) |
| Call to action, link columns, newsletter sign-up, social links | [Footer](/docs/configuration/footer/) |
| Analytics, site verification and other `<head>` tags | [Head tags](/docs/configuration/site/#head-tags) |

From the one accent color, the portal derives its text and button variants so that accent text keeps 4.5:1 contrast in both themes.

## Your own CSS

`theme.css` loads your stylesheets on every page, after the portal's own, so plain selectors win. The portal's CSS variables are the stable way in: corners, colors and spacing. See [Your own CSS](/docs/configuration/theme/#your-own-css).

## Components in guides

- **MDX**: callouts, cards, tabs, steps, badges, buttons and icons, with no imports. See [MDX](/docs/writing/mdx/).
- **Your own components**: `.mdx` pages can import Astro components (`.astro`) from your project, such as `components/Hello.astro`. See [Your own components](/docs/writing/mdx/#your-own-components).
- **Markdoc**: the same building blocks as tags, for pages that stay plain text. See [Markdoc](/docs/writing/markdoc/).
- **Live API operations** inside a guide, with Try. See [Embedding operations](/docs/writing/embedding-operations/).
- **Arazzo workflows** drawn as diagrams. See [Workflows](/docs/configuration/workflows/).

## API reference pages

Each reference page is rendered by the [RapiDoc](https://rapidocui.com) web component. The `rapidoc` key sets its attributes for every reference page: render style, schema style and expand level, Try and server selection, font size, and anything else in the [RapiDoc API reference](https://rapidocui.com/api). See [RapiDoc attributes](/docs/api-reference/rapidoc-attributes/).

## Build scripts

`@rapidoc/portal` builds, serves and checks portals from your own Node.js scripts: generate specs or pages before a build, or run several portals from one CI job. See [Programmatic API](/docs/reference/programmatic-api/).

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/configuration/customizing/

---

# Site

> Title, description, URL, logo, favicon, link previews, page titles, head tags and the announcement banner.

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
site:
  title: Acme Developers
  description: Build on the Acme payments platform.
  url: https://developers.acme.com
  logo:
    src:
      light: /logo-light.svg   # on light backgrounds
      dark: /logo-dark.svg     # on dark backgrounds
    alt: Acme
  favicon: /favicon.svg
  image: /social-card.png
  titleTemplate: '%s · Acme Developers'
  banner:
    message: API v2 is live!
    href: /docs/changelog
```

| Key | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| `title` | **Required.** The site name, in the browser tab and as the wordmark when there is no logo. |
| `description` | Default meta description of the pages. |
| `url` | Public URL of the portal, for canonical links and the sitemap. A path in it is where the portal is served; see [Serving under a path](#serving-under-a-path). `rapidoc serve` also uses it as the default external URL. |
| `logo` | The header logo; see below. |
| `favicon` | Icon in `public/`, e.g. `/favicon.svg`. |
| `image` | Preview image for links shared in Slack, X or LinkedIn (`og:image`): a file in `public/` or a URL. A file needs `url`. 1200 × 630 works best. |
| `titleTemplate` | Page titles in the browser tab and search results. `%s` is the page's own title. Default `'%s \| <title>'`. A page titled like the site shows the title alone. |
| `noindex` | `true` keeps search engines out: a robots `noindex` tag on every page, a `robots.txt` that disallows everything, and no sitemap. For staging and internal portals. |
| `banner` | An announcement bar above the header; see below. |

## Logo

One image for both themes:

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
site:
  logo:
    src: /logo.svg          # an image in public/
    text: ACME              # optional: wordmark next to the image
    alt: Acme               # optional: default the site title
    href: /                 # optional: where the logo links to (default /)
```

Or one image per theme, when the logo has dark text that would disappear on a dark background:

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
site:
  logo:
    src:
      light: /logo-light.svg   # shown in the light theme
      dark: /logo-dark.svg     # shown in the dark theme
    alt: Acme
```

The header and footer switch between the two as soon as the reader changes the theme, with no reload. This site does it: switch the theme and watch the logo.

With an image and no `text`, only the image is shown, and `alt` names it for screen readers. Without an image, the site title is the wordmark. The header shows the logo 28px tall; a wide logo shrinks on narrow screens.

The favicon is one file for both themes: pick an icon that reads on light and dark browser tabs.

## Serving under a path

When `url` has a path, the whole portal is served under it:

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
site:
  url: https://acme.com/developers   # every page is under /developers/
```

Keep writing paths as if the portal were at the root: `/docs/intro` in `navigation`, `header`, `footer`, `redirects`, `access` rules, and in links and images in your guides. The portal adds `/developers` when it builds the pages. That covers Markdown links and images, and `href`/`src` in HTML or MDX tags (`<img src="/ship.png">`). Full URLs are left alone, and so is a path built in an MDX expression (`src={...}`).

With sign-in, register `https://acme.com/developers/_rapidoc/auth/callback` at your provider. Behind a proxy that strips part of the path, see [Deploy with rapidoc serve](/docs/deploy/rapidoc-serve/#behind-a-proxy-that-strips-part-of-the-path).

## Head tags

`head` (a top-level key, next to `site`) adds tags to the `<head>` of every page: analytics, site verification, preconnects.

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
head:
  - script: { src: https://plausible.io/js/script.js, defer: true, data-domain: acme.com }
  - script: window.dataLayer = window.dataLayer || [];   # a string is an inline script
  - meta: { name: google-site-verification, content: abc123 }
  - link: { rel: preconnect, href: https://api.acme.com }
```

Each entry is one `script`, `link` or `meta` tag. Attribute values are strings, or `true` for an attribute without a value. A cookie-consent tool goes in the same way, as a script.

## Banner

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
site:
  banner:
    message: Inter-galactic shipping is live!
    href: /docs/shipping      # optional: makes the message a link
    dismissible: true         # optional: default true; readers can close it
    background: '#f76b39'     # optional: any CSS color
    color: '#000000'          # optional: text color
```

The banner sits above the header on every page.

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/configuration/site/

---

# Theme

> Accent color, light and dark mode, and fonts.

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
theme:
  primary: '#f76b39'
  mode: auto
  fonts:
    sans: { family: Inter }
    mono: { family: JetBrains Mono }
```

## Accent color

`primary` (default `#f76b39`) colors links, buttons, the active tab and sidebar item, and the API reference.

You pick one color, and the portal keeps it readable. At build time it derives the text variants from it so that accent text keeps WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1) on both the light and the dark background. Text on accent-filled buttons is black or white, whichever reads better. So a light brand color like yellow still gives readable links.

## Mode

`mode` is the theme a visitor sees until they pick one with the theme switcher:

- `auto` (default) follows the operating system.
- `light` or `dark` forces one.

Hide the switcher with `header.themeSwitcher: false`.

## Fonts

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
theme:
  fonts:
    sans: { family: Inter }                                  # loaded from Google Fonts, weights 400-700
    mono: { family: JetBrains Mono, url: /fonts/mono.css }   # your own stylesheet
```

A `family` alone loads from Google Fonts. Add `url` to load it from another CDN or from a CSS file in `public/`. `sans` is the text font; `mono` is used for code.

## Your own CSS

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
theme:
  css: ./styles/portal.css   # or a list of files
```

The files load on every page after the portal's own styles, so plain selectors win without `!important`. Paths are relative to `rapidoc.config.yaml`, and `rapidoc dev` reloads when they change.

The supported way in is the portal's CSS variables, for example:

```css title="styles/portal.css"
:root {
  --portal-radius: 0.75rem;   /* corners of cards, callouts and code blocks */
}
:root[data-theme="dark"] {
  --portal-bg: #30333c;          /* pages and sidebars */
  --portal-header-bg: #2c2d35;   /* header rows (frosted) and footer */
}
```

This site uses that to put its pages in the colors of the `amber` theme of its API reference ([below](#api-reference-colors)).

Other selectors work too, but the portal's markup can change between releases.

## API reference colors

The API reference pages follow the portal theme: the same accent color, and light or dark with the rest of the page.

To give them one of RapiDoc's [built-in themes](https://rapidocui.com/docs/theming/prebuilt-themes/) instead, with its own accent, surfaces and headings, name it under `rapidoc:`:

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
rapidoc:
  theme: amber   # ember | carbon | cobalt | jade | indigo | amber
```

The API reference pages then use the theme's colors, still light or dark with the rest of the site: the reference and its sidebar on the theme's background, the header and footer in its sidebar color, and its accent. The guides keep the portal's colors and `theme.primary`; to match them, set the same colors in [your own CSS](#your-own-css), as this site does. A `#hex` value sets only the accent, over the portal's colors. To change more of RapiDoc's look, see [RapiDoc attributes](/docs/api-reference/rapidoc-attributes/).

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/configuration/theme/

---

# Header

> The first header row - links, buttons, dropdowns, mega-menus and the theme switcher.

The header has two rows:

1. **Row 1**: the logo, the search, `header.links` and the theme switcher.
2. **Row 2**: one tab per `navigation` entry. See [Navigation](/docs/configuration/navigation/).

On narrow screens both rows collapse into the menu.

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
header:
  themeSwitcher: true
  links:
    - label: Status
      href: https://status.acme.com
    - label: Solutions
      items:
        - label: Tracking
          icon: globe
          description: Real-time tracking
          href: /docs/tracking
          items:
            - { label: Webhooks, icon: webhooks-logo, href: /docs/webhooks }
    - label: Sign up
      href: https://dashboard.acme.com/signup
      style: primary
```

## Links and buttons

A link has a `label` and an `href`. `style` makes it a button:

| `style` | Looks like |
| :--- | :--- |
| `link` (default) | Plain text link |
| `button` | Outlined button |
| `primary` | Filled button in the accent color |

Add an `icon` to show a Phosphor icon before the label.

## Dropdowns and mega-menus

A link with `items` instead of `href` opens a dropdown. When any item has an `icon` or a `description`, the dropdown becomes a mega-menu with a card per item.

Each mega-menu item can have its own `items`: shortcut links shown under it.

| Item key | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| `label`, `href` | **Required.** |
| `icon` | Phosphor icon name. |
| `description` | One line under the label. |
| `badge` | Small label next to the item: `New`, or `{ text: Beta, variant: caution }`. |
| `items` | Shortcut links: `{ label, href, icon }`. |

The menus follow the WAI-ARIA disclosure pattern: they open on click or Enter, close on Escape, and focus alone never opens them.

## Icons

Every icon name in the config is a [Phosphor](https://phosphoricons.com) icon name: `book`, `code`, `rocket`, `package`, `lightning`, `github-logo`, and so on. An unknown name shows a question mark and a build warning.

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/configuration/header/

---

# Navigation

> Header tabs and the sidebar of each documentation tab.

`navigation` is the header's second row. Each entry is a tab, and the kind of tab comes from its keys.

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
navigation:
  - label: Documentation       # documentation tab with its own sidebar
    icon: book
    items:
      - getting-started
      - label: Shipping
        items:
          - guides/first-shipment
          - { label: Ship states, href: /docs/ship-states }
      - label: Support
        collapsed: true
        autogenerate: support
  - label: Changelog           # documentation tab: every page in docs/changelog/
    autogenerate: changelog
  - label: Shipments           # API tab: one API's reference page
    icon: code
    api: shipments
  - label: API Catalog         # the catalog
    icon: squares-four
    catalog: true
  - label: Blog                # a link
    href: https://example.com/blog
```

## Tab kinds

| Key | Tab |
| :--- | :--- |
| `items` | Documentation tab; `items` is its sidebar. |
| `autogenerate: <folder>` | Documentation tab whose sidebar is every page in that folder of `docs/`. |
| `api: <id>` | The reference page of the API with that id, `/apis/<id>`. Add `version: <version>` to link to one of its [versions](/docs/api-reference/versions/) other than the default. |
| `catalog: true` | The API catalog, `/catalog`. |
| `href` | A link to another page or site. |

Every tab has a `label`, and can have an `icon` and a `badge`. Each tab must have exactly one of these keys; the build tells you when there are none or several.

## Sidebar items

Inside a documentation tab's `items`:

| Item | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| `getting-started` | A doc page by its path in `docs/`, without the extension. The label is the page title. |
| `{ label: Intro, slug: getting-started }` | The same, with your own label. |
| `{ label: Status, href: https://... }` | A link. |
| `{ label: Guides, items: [...] }` | A group. Groups nest. |
| `{ label: Support, autogenerate: support }` | A group of every page in `docs/support/`. |
| `{ label: Orders API, api: orders }` | A link to an API's reference page. Add `version: v1` for one of its [versions](/docs/api-reference/versions/). |

Groups take `collapsed: true` to start closed, and any item can have a `badge` and an `icon`, a [Phosphor](https://phosphoricons.com) icon name shown before its label:

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
navigation:
  - label: Documentation
    icon: book
    items:
      - label: Get started
        icon: rocket-launch      # any Phosphor icon name
        items:
          - { slug: getting-started, icon: lightning }
          - { label: Status, href: https://status.acme.com, icon: pulse }
```

A page needs the object form (`{ slug, icon }`) to have an icon. Pages of an `autogenerate` group have none; the group itself can.

## Which tab is active

The active tab is the one whose sidebar has the current page. Two rules decide the rest:

- Docs pages that are in no tab's sidebar belong to the **first documentation tab**.
- APIs without a tab of their own belong to the **catalog tab**.

Previous and next links at the bottom of a page stay inside the current tab.

## On small screens

Below 800px the tabs row is hidden. The menu button opens a drawer with the tabs, the header links, and the current tab's sidebar.

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/configuration/navigation/

---

# APIs

> Add OpenAPI specs to the portal - ids, titles, categories, versions and remote specs.

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
apis:
  - id: shipments
    spec: ./specs/shipments.yaml
    category: Core
  - id: billing
    spec: https://api.acme.com/billing/openapi.json
    title: Billing
    description: Invoices and payments.
    category: Finance
```

| Key | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| `id` | **Required.** Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. The reference page is `/apis/<id>`. Tabs (`api: <id>`) and embedded operations (`spec="<id>"`) refer to it. |
| `spec` | An OpenAPI 3.0, 3.1 or Swagger 2.0 file, relative to the config, or a URL. YAML or JSON. Required unless the API has `versions`. |
| `versions` | One spec per version, instead of `spec`. See [API versions](/docs/api-reference/versions/). |
| `title` | Default: `info.title` of the spec. |
| `description` | Default: `info.description` of the spec. Shown on the catalog card. |
| `category` | The group on the [catalog page](/docs/api-reference/catalog/). Default `General`. |

## What each API gets

- A reference page at `/apis/<id>`, with one page per tag below it: `/apis/<id>/<tag>`. See [Reference pages](/docs/api-reference/reference-pages/).
- A card in the catalog at `/catalog`.
- Its spec published at `/specs/<id>.<ext>`, so readers and tools can download it.
- Its operations in the site search.

## Versions

To publish several versions of one API, list a spec per version under `versions:`. The first is the default, at `/apis/<id>`; the others are at `/apis/<id>/<version>`, with a version picker on the reference page:

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
apis:
  - id: payments
    versions:
      - ./specs/payments-v3.yaml
      - ./specs/payments-v2.yaml
```

See [API versions](/docs/api-reference/versions/).

## Local or remote specs

Local specs are read at build time. Relative `$ref`s to other files resolve, and the spec is published with the site.

A remote spec (a URL) is loaded by the reader's browser from where it is hosted. The build doesn't read it, so:

- Set `title` and `description` yourself; without them the catalog shows the id.
- Its operations are not in the site search.
- `rapidoc validate` and `rapidoc mock` skip it.
- [Access rules](/docs/access/access-rules/) can't protect it. Protect it where it is hosted.

## Changing an id

The id is in every URL of the API. To keep old links working after you rename one, add a [redirect](/docs/configuration/docs-search-redirects/#redirects).

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/configuration/apis/

---

# Workflows

> Add Arazzo workflow files to the portal - drawn as diagrams in your docs, runnable from the browser, and exported as MCP tools.

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
workflows:
  - file: ./workflows/checkout.arazzo.yaml
  - id: returns
    file: ./workflows/returns-and-refunds.arazzo.yaml
    sources:
      storeAPI: orders
```

| Key | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| `file` | **Required.** An [Arazzo 1.x](https://spec.openapis.org/arazzo/latest.html) file, YAML or JSON, relative to the config. |
| `id` | Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Default: the file name without `.arazzo.yaml`. The `workflow` tag refers to it (`file="<id>"`), and the file is published at `/workflows/<id>.arazzo.yaml`. |
| `sources` | Which API in `apis:` each of the file's source descriptions is: `<source name>: <api id>`. A source whose name is already an API id needs no entry. |

## What a workflow file gets

- Its workflows can be drawn in any docs page with [`{% workflow %}`](/docs/writing/markdoc/#workflow): a diagram of the steps, the values passed between them and the success and failure actions, generated at build time.
- **Run workflow** on that diagram runs the steps from the reader's browser against the servers in the specs, with the credentials the reader types in.
- The portal's MCP export turns each workflow into one tool, with the workflow's inputs as the tool's arguments.

## Sources

An Arazzo file names the APIs it uses in `sourceDescriptions`. The portal resolves each source to one of your APIs and reads the operations from that API's spec (its default [version](/docs/api-reference/versions/)), so the `url` in the file does not have to be reachable at build time:

```yaml title="workflows/checkout.arazzo.yaml"
sourceDescriptions:
  - name: orders            # an API id: resolves to apis[].id "orders"
    url: ../specs/orders.yaml
    type: openapi
  - name: storeAPI          # not an API id: map it in sources
    url: https://example.com/store.json
    type: openapi
```

The `url` still matters when a reader runs the workflow from a docs page: the first source is replaced by the API's published spec, and the others are fetched relative to the published workflow file. Writing them relative to the file (`../specs/orders.yaml`) works both on disk and once published.

## Run against the mock

**Run workflow** sends each step's request to the first server of that step's API, from the reader's browser. List [`rapidoc mock`](/docs/tools/mock-server/) first in each spec's `servers`, and every workflow on your docs pages runs with no backend:

```yaml title="specs/orders.yaml"
servers:
  - url: http://localhost:4010/orders
    description: Mock server (rapidoc mock)
  - url: https://api.acme.com/v1
```

```bash
npx rapidoc mock
```

A workflow that spans several APIs works the same way: each API answers under its own `/<api id>`.

- **Credentials**: the run panel has one field per security scheme of the workflow's APIs. Values stay in the page. Started with `--issuer`, the mock checks a pasted token's signature, audience and scopes, so a step the reader isn't allowed to call fails with `403`, and the workflow follows its `onFailure` actions.
- **Failure paths**: the mock answers each operation's documented success response. To walk a failure branch, open **Mock Response Status** in the run panel and give a step the status it should get (`404`, or `503, 200` for a first attempt that fails and a retry that succeeds); the run sends it to the mock as `Prefer: code=<status>`.
- **Before you publish**: move the real server first, or the published portal runs workflows against `localhost`.

## Checks

`rapidoc validate`, `rapidoc dev` and `rapidoc build` warn about a workflow the runtime cannot run and leave it out of the MCP export: a step whose operation is not in the API's spec, a source that matches no API, a step that calls another workflow, or `regex`, `jsonpath` and `xpath` criteria (only simple conditions such as `$statusCode == 200` run for now). The diagram still draws such a workflow.

## Access

With [sign-in and access rules](/docs/access/overview/), a workflow file follows its APIs: it is public when every API it uses is public, else it is served from the zone of the first API that is not.

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/configuration/workflows/

---

# Footer

> Call to action, link columns, newsletter sign-up, social links and copyright.

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
footer:
  cta:
    title: Ready to ship?
    description: Book your first shipment in minutes.
    links:
      - { label: Get started, href: /docs/quickstart }
      - { label: Contact sales, href: /contact }
  newsletter:
    action: https://example.us1.list-manage.com/subscribe/post?u=...
    field: EMAIL
  columns:
    - title: Company
      links:
        - { label: About, href: /about }
        - { label: Careers, href: /careers }
  social:
    - { icon: github, href: https://github.com/acme }
    - { icon: discord, href: https://discord.gg/acme }
  copyright: © 2026 Acme, Inc.
  branding: true
```

Set `footer: false` to have no footer.

## Call to action

`cta` is a band at the top of the footer with a `title`, an optional `description` and up to three `links`. The first link is a filled button and the others are outlined; set `style: primary` or `style: button` on a link to choose.

## Newsletter

`newsletter` adds an email sign-up form under the footer logo. The form posts to `action`, your newsletter service's form endpoint (Mailchimp, Buttondown, ConvertKit, ...).

| Key | Default |
| :--- | :--- |
| `action` | **Required.** The URL the form posts to. |
| `field` | `email`. The name of the email field your service expects. |
| `title` | `Newsletter` |
| `description` | none |
| `button` | `Subscribe` |

## Columns, social links, copyright

- `columns`: groups of links, each with a `title`.
- `social`: icons for `github`, `x`, `discord`, `linkedin` and `youtube`.
- `copyright`: one line of text.
- `branding`: shows "Powered by RapiDoc". Default `true`.

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/configuration/footer/

---

# Docs, search and redirects

> The docs folder, table of contents, edit links, site search and redirects.

## Docs

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
docs:
  dir: ./docs
  toc: { minHeadingLevel: 2, maxHeadingLevel: 3 }
  editUrl: https://github.com/acme/portal/edit/main/docs/
```

| Key | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| `dir` | Folder with the `.md`, `.mdx` and `.markdoc` pages. Default `./docs`. |
| `toc` | The headings shown in "On this page". Default levels 2 to 3. `false` hides it. |
| `editUrl` | Base URL of the docs folder in your repository. Each page gets an "Edit page" link to `<editUrl><path of the page>`. |

A page can override the table of contents in its frontmatter with the `tableOfContents` key (see [Markdown](/docs/writing/markdown/#title-and-frontmatter)).

## Search

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
search: true   # default
```

The search box in the header searches guides and API operations. Both indexes are built with the site, so there is no search service to run or pay for: guides are indexed by [Pagefind](https://pagefind.app), and every operation's method, path, summary and description go into a second index.

Press `/` or `Ctrl K` (`⌘ K` on a Mac) to open it. With [access rules](/docs/access/access-rules/), readers only find what they may read.

Set `search: false` to remove the search box.

## Redirects

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
redirects:
  - { from: /old-page, to: /docs/new-page }
  - { from: /docs/v1/auth, to: https://legacy.acme.com/auth }
```

Each redirect is a page at `from` that sends readers to `to`. Use them when you move a page or rename an API id. `rapidoc migrate` writes redirects for APIs that had a custom path in your old portal.

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/configuration/docs-search-redirects/

---

# LLM output

> Every guide as Markdown, /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt for AI tools, and Copy page buttons.

AI assistants and coding agents read documentation better as Markdown than as HTML. The portal publishes it for them, with nothing to configure:

| URL | Content |
| :--- | :--- |
| `/docs/<page>.md` | Each guide as Markdown. The home page is `/index.md`. |
| `/llms.txt` | An index ([llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org)): the site, then the pages of each documentation tab, then every API with its OpenAPI file. |
| `/llms-full.txt` | Every guide's Markdown in one file. |

Try it on this site: [/llms.txt](/llms.txt), or [this page as Markdown](/docs/configuration/llms.md).

## Page actions

Next to the title of each guide:

- **Copy page** copies the page as Markdown, ready to paste into a chat.
- **View as Markdown** opens the `.md` file.
- **Open in ChatGPT** and **Open in Claude** start a conversation that reads the page.

## Settings

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
llms:
  description: Build on the Acme payments platform.   # top of /llms.txt (default site.description)
  pageActions: [copy, markdown, chatgpt, claude]      # default all four; false hides the buttons
```

`llms: false` turns all of it off: no `.md` files, no `llms.txt`, no buttons.

## How guides become Markdown

Guides are converted from their source, so the Markdown stays close to what you wrote:

- Frontmatter and MDX `import` lines are removed; the title and description become the first lines.
- Callouts (`:::note`, `{% callout %}`, `<Aside>`) become quotes: `> **Note:** ...`.
- `{% api-operation %}` becomes the method and path, with a link to the API page.
- Cards become linked titles, tabs and steps keep their labels, and other tags keep their text.
- Code blocks and inline code are left exactly as written.

## With sign-in

- `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt` list **public pages only**, and only public APIs.
- A protected page's `.md` is protected like the page: an access rule for `/docs/internal/**` covers `/docs/internal/runbook.md`.
- On protected pages, **Open in ChatGPT** and **Open in Claude** are hidden: an assistant can't sign in to read the page. **Copy page** and **View as Markdown** still work for the signed-in reader.

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/configuration/llms/

---

# Markdown

> Write guides in plain Markdown - titles, frontmatter, links, images and code.

Plain Markdown (`.md`) is the simplest way to write a guide. Every file in `docs/` is a page. Pick a format per page: Markdown, [Markdoc](/docs/writing/markdoc/) or [MDX](/docs/writing/mdx/) can sit side by side.

## Title and frontmatter

```markdown title="docs/authentication.md"
---
title: Authentication
description: Get an access token and send it with every request.
---

Every request needs an access token...
```

Without a `title` in the frontmatter, a first `# Heading` becomes the page title. So a README-style file works as-is:

```markdown title="docs/authentication.md"
# Authentication

Every request needs an access token...
```

These frontmatter keys work too:

| Key | Does |
| :--- | :--- |
| `description` | The page's description, used by search engines and link previews. |
| `sidebar` | The page's sidebar link: `label`, `order` and `badge`. |
| `tableOfContents` | Overrides `docs.toc` for this page. `false` hides "On this page". |
| `template: splash` | A full-width page without sidebars, for a landing page. |
| `hero` | A title block with a tagline, an image and action links, for a landing page. See [Landing pages](#landing-pages). |
| `draft` | `true` leaves the page out of `rapidoc build`. |
| `pagefind` | `false` keeps the page out of search. |

## Landing pages

A page with `template: splash` and a `hero` is a landing page, like this site's home page. Any page in `docs/` can be one; point a [link tab](/docs/configuration/navigation/) at it to give it its own tab.

```markdown title="docs/solutions.md"
---
title: Solutions
template: splash
hero:
  layout: stacked
  title: Ship faster with<br><mark>our APIs</mark>
  tagline: Prices, bookings and tracking for every parcel.
  image:
    html: <img src="/images/hero.png" alt="A booked shipment and its tracking timeline" width="520" height="460">
  actions:
    - text: Get started
      link: /docs/getting-started/quickstart/
    - text: Browse the APIs
      link: /catalog/
      variant: secondary
---
```

| Key | Does |
| :--- | :--- |
| `hero.title` | The large heading; without it, the page `title`. Inline HTML works: `<br>` breaks the line, `<mark>` shows gradient text. |
| `hero.tagline` | The text under the heading. Inline HTML works. |
| `hero.image` | `html`: an `<img>` of a file in `public/`, or an inline SVG. Starlight's `file`, `dark` and `light` keys take a path relative to the page. |
| `hero.actions` | Buttons: `text`, `link`, `variant` (`primary`, `secondary` or `minimal`) and `icon`. |
| `hero.layout` | `split` (default): the text left and the image right; without an image the text takes the full width. `stacked`: the text and buttons centred, the image below them. |

On phones both layouts are one column, with the image below the text.

## Links

Link to other guides by URL: `[Errors](/docs/errors/)`. Link to an API reference page with `/apis/<id>`, to one tag with `/apis/<id>/<tag>`, and to one operation with its anchor:

```markdown
See [Create a shipment](/apis/shipments/shipments#create-shipment).
```

## Images

Put images in `public/` and use their path from the site root:

```markdown
![Label example](/images/label.png)
```

## Code

Fenced code blocks are highlighted by [Expressive Code](https://expressive-code.com), with a copy button. Add a title, mark lines, or show a terminal frame:

````markdown
```js title="client.js" {2}
const res = await fetch('https://api.acme.com/v1/orders', {
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
});
```

```bash
npm install @acme/sdk
```
````

## Callouts

Highlight a note, tip or warning with a `:::` block:

```markdown
:::tip[Use idempotency keys]
Retrying a POST with the same key never creates a second order.
:::
```

> **Tip: Use idempotency keys**
> Retrying a POST with the same key never creates a second order.

More types and options: [Callouts](/docs/writing/callouts/).

## Tables, lists, and the rest

GitHub-flavored Markdown works: tables, task lists, strikethrough, autolinks and footnotes.

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/writing/markdown/

---

# Markdoc

> Markdoc tags for callouts, tabs, steps, cards, badges and live API operations.

[Markdoc](https://markdoc.dev) is Markdown with tags. Name the file `.markdoc`. Headings, the table of contents and code blocks work as in Markdown, and these tags add components. Each example below shows the source, then the result.

## Callout

```markdoc
{% callout type="tip" title="Good to know" %}
Sandbox keys start with `sk_test_`.
{% /callout %}
```

> **Tip: Good to know**
> Sandbox keys start with `sk_test_`.

`type` is one of `note`, `info`, `tip`, `success`, `caution`, `warning`, `danger`, `sparkles`, `rocket`, `settings`, `zap`, `lock`, `megaphone`. `icon` picks any other [Phosphor](https://phosphoricons.com) icon. See [Callouts](/docs/writing/callouts/).

## Tabs

````markdoc
{% tabs %}
{% tab name="npm" %}
```bash
npm install @acme/sdk
```
{% /tab %}
{% tab name="pnpm" %}
```bash
pnpm add @acme/sdk
```
{% /tab %}
{% /tabs %}
````

**npm**

```bash
npm install @acme/sdk
```

**pnpm**

```bash
pnpm add @acme/sdk
```

## Steps

```markdoc
{% steps %}
{% step title="Get a key" %}
Create an API key in the dashboard.
{% /step %}
{% step title="Call the API" %}
Send it in the `Authorization` header.
{% /step %}
{% /steps %}
```

**Get a key**

Create an API key in the dashboard.

**Call the API**

Send it in the `Authorization` header.

## Cards

```markdoc
{% card-grid columns=2 %}
{% card title="Quickstart" icon="rocket" href="/docs/getting-started/quickstart" %}
A portal in five minutes.
{% /card %}
{% card title="Example API" icon="code" href="/apis/bookstore" %}
See a reference page.
{% /card %}
{% /card-grid %}
```

**[Quickstart](/docs/getting-started/quickstart)**

A portal in five minutes.

**[Example API](/apis/bookstore)**

See a reference page.

`columns` defaults to 3. `href` makes the whole card a link; `icon` is a Phosphor icon name.

## Badge

```markdoc
Webhooks {% badge text="Beta" variant="caution" /%}
```

Webhooks Beta

## API operation

```markdoc
{% api-operation spec="bookstore" path="/books/{bookId}" method="get" /%}
```

`GET /books/{bookId}` ([Bookstore API](/apis/bookstore))

Embeds one live operation from an API in `apis:`. See [Embedding operations](/docs/writing/embedding-operations/).

## Workflow

```markdoc
{% workflow file="bookstore" id="findBook" title="Find a book" /%}
```

Draws one workflow of a file in [`workflows:`](/docs/configuration/workflows/): `file` is the entry's id, `id` the `workflowId` in the file (default: its first workflow), `view` is `expanded` (the default) or `compact`, and `title` a caption. The tag shows the workflow runner: the diagram with a panel for the inputs and credentials, and **Run workflow** executes the steps from the browser. The same diagram is also generated at build time, so it shows while the runner loads and without JavaScript.

## More tags

| Tag | Does |
| :--- | :--- |
| `aside` | The same as `callout`. |
| `linkcard` | A card that links to a page: `title`, `href` and an optional `description`. |
| `linkbutton` | A link drawn as a button: `href`, and `variant` (`primary`, `secondary`, `minimal`). |
| `filetree` | A folder tree, drawn from the nested list inside it. |

## Showing tag source in a code block

A code fence shows its content as text, tags included, so the examples on this page are plain fences. Markdoc still checks the tags inside a fence, though: an unknown tag or attribute fails the build even inside a code block.

To show tags that aren't valid here, such as a tag from another site or a made-up example, turn the check off with Markdoc's `process=false` annotation after the language:

````markdoc {% process=false %}
```markdoc {% process=false %}
{% my-own-tag color="teal" %}Shown as text, never checked.{% /my-own-tag %}
```
````

Code fences in `markdoc` are highlighted as Markdown.

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/writing/markdoc/

---

# MDX

> Use components in guides with MDX - no imports needed for the portal components.

[MDX](https://mdxjs.com) is Markdown with JSX components. Name the file `.mdx`.

## Components without imports

These portal components work in any `.mdx` page without an `import`: the build adds it for you.

| Component | Use |
| :--- | :--- |
| `<Callout type="tip" title="...">` | A callout; same types as [Callouts](/docs/writing/callouts/). |
| `<Card>`, `<CardHeader>`, `<CardTitle>`, `<CardDescription>`, `<CardContent>`, `<CardFooter>` | Card building blocks. |
| `<Badge text="Beta" variant="caution" />` | A small label. |
| `<Button href="/docs/quickstart" variant="default">` | A link styled as a button. Variants: `default`, `outline`, `secondary`, `ghost`; sizes `sm`, `md`, `lg`. |
| `<Link href="...">` | A link. |
| `<Steps>` | Numbered steps around an ordered list. |
| `<Tabs>`, `<TabItem label="...">` | Tabs. |
| `<OpenPlaygroundButton>` | A button that opens an API playground. |

```mdx title="docs/webhooks.mdx"
---
title: Webhooks
---

<Callout type="caution" title="Verify every request">
  Check the signature header before you trust a webhook.
</Callout>

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="Node.js">...</TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Python">...</TabItem>
</Tabs>
```

## Components and icons

The components `Aside`, `CardGrid`, `LinkCard`, `LinkButton`, `FileTree` and `Icon` are exported from `@rapidoc/portal/components`. Import the ones you use:

```mdx
import { CardGrid, LinkCard, Icon } from '@rapidoc/portal/components';

<Icon name="rocket" /> Ready?

<CardGrid>
  <LinkCard title="Quickstart" href="/docs/getting-started/quickstart" />
  <LinkCard title="Example API" href="/apis/bookstore" />
</CardGrid>
```

`Icon` draws a [Phosphor](https://phosphoricons.com) icon at 24px; `size={16}` makes it smaller. The portal uses Phosphor icons only, so icons in guides match the header and sidebar.

## Your own components

An `.mdx` page can import Astro components (`.astro` files) and JavaScript modules from your project, for example from a `components/` folder next to `docs/`. Import them with a path relative to the page:

```astro title="components/Hello.astro"
---
const { name = "world" } = Astro.props;
---

<p class="hello">Hello, {name}!</p>

<style>
  .hello { font-weight: 600; }
</style>
```

```mdx title="docs/welcome.mdx"
---
title: Welcome
---

import Hello from '../components/Hello.astro';

<Hello name="developer" />
```

A component can import other components and use the portal's, and its `<style>` is scoped to it as in any Astro project. `rapidoc dev` reloads the page when you edit the component.

React, Vue and Svelte components (`.jsx`, `.tsx`, `.vue`, `.svelte`) are not supported: the build stops with an error that names the page and the import. Write the markup as an `.astro` component instead; a `<script>` in it can add behaviour in the browser.

## Migrated Zudoku pages

Imports from `zudoku/ui/...` and the `<Stepper>` component are rewritten automatically, so MDX pages from a Zudoku project work as-is. See [Migrating](/docs/tools/migrate/).

## Markdown or MDX?

If both `page.md` and `page.mdx` exist, the `.mdx` one is used. Prefer Markdown or Markdoc for prose: they don't break when a `<` or `{` appears in the text, which MDX treats as code.

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/writing/mdx/

---

# Callouts

> Notes, tips and warnings - one look whether you write them in Markdown, MDX or Markdoc.

A callout looks the same whichever way you write it, so pick the syntax of the page's format.

| Format | Syntax |
| :--- | :--- |
| Markdown, MDX | `:::tip` ... `:::` |
| MDX | `<Callout type="tip">` or `<Aside type="tip">` |
| Markdoc | `{% callout type="tip" %}` or `{% aside type="tip" %}` |

## Markdown blocks

```markdown
:::note
A plain note.
:::

:::caution[Rate limits]
More than 100 requests a second get a 429.
:::

:::danger{title="Irreversible"}
Deleting an account removes all its data.
:::
```

> **Note:**
> A plain note.

> **Caution: Rate limits**
> More than 100 requests a second get a 429.

> **Danger: Irreversible**
> Deleting an account removes all its data.

The title goes in square brackets, `:::tip[Title]`, or in braces, `:::tip{title="Title"}`.

## Types

| Type | Icon |
| :--- | :--- |
| `note`, `info` | info |
| `tip` | lightbulb |
| `success` | check circle |
| `caution`, `warning` | warning |
| `danger` | shield warning |
| `sparkles` | sparkle |
| `rocket` | rocket |
| `settings` | gear |
| `zap` | lightning |
| `lock` | lock |
| `megaphone` | megaphone |

Zudoku's names (`info`, `warning`, `sparkles`, ...) work too, so migrated pages render as they did.

> **Note: New in v2**
> The `rocket`, `sparkles`, `zap` and `megaphone` types suit announcements.

## Another icon

`icon` picks any [Phosphor](https://phosphoricons.com) icon:

```mdx
<Callout type="info" icon="clock" title="Takes a few minutes">
  Label generation runs in the background.
</Callout>
```

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/writing/callouts/

---

# Embedding operations

> Put a live, interactive API operation inside a guide.

A guide that explains an endpoint can show the endpoint itself: its parameters, request body, responses, and a **Try** console. Embed one with the `api-operation` Markdoc tag:

```markdoc
{% api-operation spec="bookstore" path="/orders" method="post" title="Place an order" /%}
```

`POST /orders` Place an order ([Bookstore API](/apis/bookstore))

## Attributes

| Attribute | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| `spec` | **Required.** The `id` of an API in `apis:`. |
| `path` | **Required.** The path as written in the spec, with its `{parameters}`. |
| `method` | `get` (default), `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, ... |
| `title` | A heading for the embed. Default: the operation's summary. |
| `version` | One of the API's [versions](/docs/api-reference/versions/). Default: its default version. |
| `collapsed` | `true` shows only the method and path; the reader clicks them to open the operation. Default `false`. |

An unknown `spec` id shows a notice on the page and a build warning, so a typo doesn't go unnoticed.

## Collapsed embeds

A guide that lists several operations stays short with `collapsed=true`. Each one shows its method and path, and opens in place when clicked:

```markdoc
{% api-operation spec="bookstore" path="/books" title="List books" collapsed=true /%}
```

`GET /books` List books ([Bookstore API](/apis/bookstore))

## How it works

The embed is RapiDoc's `<rapi-doc-mini>` element showing one operation of the spec. It follows the portal theme and accent color.

Only pages with an embed load the RapiDoc bundle. Other docs pages stay light.

## Try from a guide

**Try** sends a real request to the spec's server. In this site's example spec, the server is the local mock: run `npm run mock:portal-site` in the [RapiDoc repository](https://github.com/rapi-doc/RapiDoc), where this site's source is (`sites/rapi-portal`), and the console above answers. See [Mock server](/docs/tools/mock-server/).

With sign-in and `auth.tryIt`, the embed fills in the signed-in reader's access token. See [Try with the reader's token](/docs/access/try-it/).

## In MDX or Markdown

The tag is Markdoc only. In an `.md` or `.mdx` guide, link to the operation on its reference page instead: `/apis/bookstore/orders#create-order`.

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/writing/embedding-operations/

---

# Reference pages

> What each API's reference page shows, its URLs, and how to link to an operation.

Every API in `apis:` gets an interactive reference page, rendered by the [RapiDoc](https://rapidocui.com) web component. See one: [the example Bookstore API](/apis/bookstore/).

## URLs

| URL | Shows |
| :--- | :--- |
| `/apis/<id>` | The API's overview: title, description, servers, authentication. |
| `/apis/<id>/<tag>` | The operations of one tag. One page per tag keeps big APIs fast. |
| `/apis/<id>/<tag>#<operation>` | One operation. The anchor is the `operationId` in kebab-case: `createOrder` is `#create-order`. |
| `/apis` | Redirects to the [catalog](/docs/api-reference/catalog/). |
| `/specs/<id>.yaml` | The spec itself (or `.json`, the file's own extension). |

Tag slugs are the tag names in kebab-case: the tag `Shipment Management` is `/apis/shipments/shipment-management`.

An API with [versions](/docs/api-reference/versions/) has these URLs for its default version, and the same below `/apis/<id>/<version>` for each other version.

## The page

- **A version picker** at the top of the sidebar, when the API has [several versions](/docs/api-reference/versions/).
- **A sidebar** on the left lists the tags and their operations, with the HTTP method of each. It is static HTML, so it shows at once, before the reference has loaded, and it stays in view while the page scrolls. Its filter box narrows the list as you type.
- **The reference** shows each operation's parameters, request body, responses and examples, with schemas as an expandable tree or a table.
- **Try** sends a real request to the spec's server from the reader's browser and shows the response.
- **Authentication** lets readers enter an API key, a bearer token, or sign in with OAuth 2 before they try.

The page follows the portal: same header, footer, theme and accent color, and light or dark with the rest of the site.

## Linking to an operation

Give every operation an `operationId`. The anchor is then stable:

```markdown
[Create a shipment](/apis/shipments/shipments#create-shipment)
```

Without an `operationId`, the anchor is built from the summary and changes when the summary is edited, so `rapidoc dev` and `rapidoc build` warn about such operations. Every operation can also be linked by its method and path, which only changes with the endpoint: `#get-orders-orderid`.

## OAuth 2 sign-in for Try

Readers can sign in to your API from the API reference page and call it with **Try**, using their own account. The sign-in runs in the browser, so it works on a plain [static](/docs/deploy/static-hosting/) portal: no `auth` key and no `rapidoc serve`. It covers calls to your API only; the documentation stays public.

### How it works

1. The spec declares an `oauth2` or `openIdConnect` security scheme. RapiDoc shows it in the page's **Authentication** section.
2. The reader presses **Authorize**. RapiDoc opens your provider's sign-in in a popup, using the authorization code flow with PKCE.
3. The provider redirects the popup to `/oauth-receiver.html`, a page every portal build has. It hands the code back to the API page, and RapiDoc exchanges it for an access token at the `tokenUrl`.
4. **Try** sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to your API. The token stays in the page's memory and is gone on reload.

### Declare the scheme

Use a standard OpenAPI `oauth2` scheme. For a public client, pre-fill the client ID with `x-client-id` and set `x-pkce-only: true`, which hides the client secret fields, so readers only press **Authorize**:

```yaml title="specs/orders.yaml"
components:
  securitySchemes:
    OAuth:
      type: oauth2
      flows:
        authorizationCode:
          authorizationUrl: https://acme.okta.com/oauth2/default/v1/authorize
          tokenUrl: https://acme.okta.com/oauth2/default/v1/token
          scopes:
            orders:read: Read your orders
            orders:write: Create and change orders
          x-client-id: portal-try
          x-pkce-only: true
          x-default-scopes: [orders:read]
security:
  - OAuth: [orders:read]
```

More extensions, such as `x-authorize-params` and `x-token-params` for an `audience`, are in RapiDoc's [OAuth guide](https://rapidocui.com/docs/authentication/oauth/).

### At your provider

- Register a **single-page application** (a public client: authorization code with PKCE, no client secret). A secret in a static page is readable by anyone.
- Add `<portal URL>/oauth-receiver.html` as a redirect URL: one URL for the whole portal. For local testing, add `http://localhost:4321/oauth-receiver.html` too.
- Allow the portal's origin for CORS on the token endpoint: the browser calls it directly. Most providers do this for single-page-app clients.
- Your API must also allow the portal's origin for CORS, as for any **Try** request.

### Browser sign-in or portal sign-in

| | Browser sign-in (this section) | [Portal sign-in](/docs/access/overview/) with [`tryIt`](/docs/access/try-it/) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Hosting | Any static host | `rapidoc serve` |
| Provider set in | The spec's security scheme | The portal config (`auth`) |
| Protects the documentation | No | Yes, with `access` rules |
| Readers sign in | Once per API, with **Authorize** | Once for the whole portal; **Try** has their token |

With portal sign-in and `tryIt`, readers don't need to authorize separately.

## Customizing

Change how RapiDoc renders, such as the schema style, the code sample languages or the font size, with the `rapidoc:` key. See [RapiDoc attributes](/docs/api-reference/rapidoc-attributes/).

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/api-reference/reference-pages/

---

# API versions

> Publish several versions of one API, each with its own URLs, and a version picker on the reference page.

An API can have one spec per version. Each version gets its own reference pages, and a version picker at the top of the API's sidebar switches between them. Readers land on the current version; older ones stay one click away.

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
apis:
  - id: payments
    title: Payments API
    versions:
      - spec: ./specs/payments-v3.yaml
        version: v3
        label: v3 (latest)
      - spec: ./specs/payments-v2.yaml
        version: v2
      - ./specs/payments-v1.yaml
```

Use `versions:` instead of `spec:`: an API has one or the other. **The first version is the default.**

| Key | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| `spec` | **Required.** The OpenAPI file of this version, relative to the config, or a URL. |
| `version` | The version's part of the URL: lowercase letters, digits, dots and dashes (`v2`, `2.1.0`, `2024-06-01`). Default: `info.version` of the spec. Required when `spec` is a URL. |
| `label` | The text in the version picker. Default: `info.version` of the spec. |

A version can also be just the path of its spec, like `./specs/payments-v1.yaml` above: its `version` and `label` both come from the spec's `info.version`. If that isn't a valid URL part (`Version 1`, say), the build asks you to set `version`.

`title`, `description` and `category` belong to the API, not a version. Their defaults come from the spec of the default version.

## URLs

| URL | Shows |
| :--- | :--- |
| `/apis/<id>`, `/apis/<id>/<tag>` | The default version. |
| `/apis/<id>/<version>`, `/apis/<id>/<version>/<tag>` | Every other version. |
| `/apis/<id>/<default version>/...` | Redirects to the same page without the version, and keeps the `#operation`. |

So `/apis/payments` always shows the current version, and existing links keep working when you add versions. A link that names a version, such as `/apis/payments/v3/charges`, keeps working too: while v3 is the default it redirects to `/apis/payments/charges`, and once v4 takes over it is v3's own page.

A version can't have the same name as a tag page of the default version: `version: refunds` next to a default version with a `Refunds` tag would share `/apis/payments/refunds`, and the build stops with an error.

## The version picker

The picker sits at the top of the API's sidebar, above the endpoint filter, when the API has more than one version. Choosing a version opens the same tag, and the same operation, in that version when it has the tag, and the version's overview when it doesn't.

Pages of a version other than the default start with a note that names the current version and links to it.

## Specs

The default version's spec is published at `/specs/<id>.<ext>`, as for an API with one spec. Every version is also at `/specs/<id>/<version>.<ext>`, so a tool that needs one version, such as a client generator, has a URL that doesn't change when the default does.

## Navigation, catalog, search and embeds

- **Navigation**: `api: payments` links to the default version. Add `version:` to link to another one, for example a tab for an older version that many readers still use:

  ```yaml
  navigation:
    - label: Payments
      api: payments
    - label: Payments v2
      api: payments
      version: v2
  ```

  A tab for one version is the current tab on that version's pages; the API's other pages belong to its main tab.
- **Catalog**: one card per API, linking to the default version and showing its label and how many versions there are.
- **Search**: finds operations of every version. Results from a version other than the default say which version they are from.
- **Embedded operations**: `{% api-operation spec="payments" ... /%}` shows the operation from the default version; add `version="v2"` for another one. See [Embedding operations](/docs/writing/embedding-operations/).

## Access rules

A rule on `/apis/<id>/**` covers every version of the API and every version's spec. To protect only one version, for example a beta, write a rule for its URLs:

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
access:
  rules:
    - path: /apis/payments/v4-beta/**
      allow:
        groups: [beta-testers]
```

Each spec follows the pages of its version, so `/specs/payments/v4-beta.yaml` is protected with them. See [Access rules](/docs/access/access-rules/).

## Coming from Zudoku

`rapidoc migrate --from zudoku` turns an `input` list into `versions:`: plain paths stay paths, and `{ path, label, input }` becomes `{ version, label, spec }`. Old version URLs get redirects. A `?prefix=` input, which shows part of one file as a version, isn't supported: the migration drops the query and warns. See [Migrate](/docs/tools/migrate/).

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/api-reference/versions/

---

# API catalog

> The /catalog page - every API, grouped by category.

`/catalog` lists every API of the portal as a card, grouped by `category`. Each card shows the API's title, version and description, and links to its reference page.

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
apis:
  - id: shipments
    spec: ./specs/shipments.yaml
    category: Shipping
  - id: tracking
    spec: ./specs/tracking.yaml
    category: Shipping
  - id: billing
    spec: ./specs/billing.yaml
    category: Finance
```

| Card | Comes from |
| :--- | :--- |
| Title | `title` in `apis:`, else `info.title` of the spec |
| Version | `info.version` of the spec. For an API with [versions](/docs/api-reference/versions/): the default version's label and how many versions there are. |
| Description | `description` in `apis:`, else `info.description` of the spec |
| Group | `category` in `apis:`, default `General` |

## A tab for the catalog

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
navigation:
  - label: API Catalog
    icon: squares-four
    catalog: true
```

APIs that don't have a tab of their own belong to the catalog tab: on their reference pages, the catalog tab is the active one.

`/apis` always redirects to `/catalog`.

## With access rules

APIs a reader may not open stay in the catalog with a lock icon, so readers know they exist and can sign in. See [Access rules](/docs/access/access-rules/).

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/api-reference/catalog/

---

# RapiDoc attributes

> Change how API reference pages render with the rapidoc key.

The reference pages are the `<rapi-doc>` web component. The `rapidoc:` key sets its attributes for every API reference page:

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
rapidoc:
  render-style: read        # read | view | focused
  schema-style: tree        # tree | table
  default-schema-tab: example
  schema-expand-level: 2
  allow-server-selection: true
  font-size: largest
```

Values are strings, numbers or booleans. Every attribute is described in the [RapiDoc API reference](https://rapidocui.com/api). `theme` picks one of RapiDoc's built-in themes for the reference pages (see [API reference colors](/docs/configuration/theme/#api-reference-colors)).

## Portal defaults

Without a `rapidoc:` key, the portal uses:

| Attribute | Default |
| :--- | :--- |
| `render-style` | `read` |
| `schema-style` | `table` |
| `scale` | `default` |
| `allow-try` | `true` |
| `allow-authentication` | `true` |
| `allow-server-selection` | `false` |
| `show-method-in-nav-bar` | `as-colored-text` |
| `use-path-in-nav-bar` | `false` |

Your `rapidoc:` values replace these.

## The API sidebar

The sidebar of an API reference page is drawn by the portal, not by `<rapi-doc>` (its own navigation is hidden). Two navigation attributes still apply to it:

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
rapidoc:
  show-method-in-nav-bar: as-colored-block  # as-colored-text (default) | as-colored-block | as-plain-text | false
  use-path-in-nav-bar: true                 # show each operation's path instead of its summary
```

| `show-method-in-nav-bar` | Shows |
| :--- | :--- |
| `as-colored-text` | The method in its color: `GET`, `POST`, `DELETE`. |
| `as-colored-block` | A colored three-letter badge: `GET`, `POS`, `DEL`. |
| `as-plain-text` | The method in the text color. |
| `false` | No method. |

Other navigation attributes, such as `nav-item-spacing` or `nav-bg-color`, have no effect: change the sidebar's look with [your own CSS](/docs/configuration/theme/#your-own-css).

## Attributes the portal sets itself

Some attributes are part of the portal's layout, so setting them under `rapidoc:` is an error. The message names the key to use instead:

| Attribute | Use instead |
| :--- | :--- |
| `spec-url` | `apis[].spec` |
| `primary-color` | `theme.primary` |
| `color-scheme` | `theme.mode` |
| `show-header`, `show-side-nav` | (the portal draws its own header and sidebar) |
| `update-route`, `goto-path`, `auto-height`, `oauth-receiver` | (set by the page) |

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/api-reference/rapidoc-attributes/

---

# Single sign-on (SSO)

> Put the portal behind your company's single sign-on (SSO) with OpenID Connect (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google, Keycloak, Auth0), and decide who may read which pages and APIs.

When some guides or APIs are only for partners, customers or your own staff, readers can sign in with your company's single sign-on (SSO): Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Keycloak, Auth0, AWS Cognito, Ping, Authentik, Zitadel or any other OpenID Connect provider. SAML-only providers work through a broker ([Identity providers](/docs/access/providers/#saml-only-providers)).

This page explains the parts and how to choose. To set it up, follow [Set up sign-in](/docs/access/setup/), or [SSO with Microsoft Entra ID](/docs/access/entra-id/) for every Entra ID screen.

Add two keys to `rapidoc.config.yaml`:

- `auth`: readers sign in through your OpenID Connect provider.
- `access`: rules that decide who may read which pages, APIs and files.

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
auth:
  issuer: https://acme.okta.com/oauth2/default
  clientId: portal-web
  scopes: [openid, profile, email, groups]

access:
  default: public
  rules:
    - path: /docs/partners/**
      allow: signed-in
    - path: /apis/billing/**
      allow: { groups: [billing-team] }
```

## Choose your setup

| You need | Setup |
| :--- | :--- |
| Some pages or APIs public, others only for some readers or groups | `auth` and `access`, served by `rapidoc serve`. |
| The whole portal private, every signed-in reader sees everything, with a sign-in button, per-reader search, and **Try** or agents using the reader's token | `auth` with `access.default: signed-in`, served by `rapidoc serve`. |
| The whole portal private, nothing more | A plain static build behind your SSO proxy, with no portal server ([Static hosting](/docs/deploy/static-hosting/#the-whole-portal-behind-your-sso)). |
| Only calls to your API need a sign-in; the docs stay public | No `auth`: readers sign in from the API page ([OAuth 2 sign-in for Try](/docs/api-reference/reference-pages/#oauth-2-sign-in-for-try)). |

[Try with the reader's token](/docs/access/try-it/) is optional: it is for portals whose API accepts tokens from the same provider.

> **Caution: Who counts as "signed in"**
> `signed-in` lets in everyone your provider lets sign in, not only your employees. Depending on how the provider is set up, that can include anyone with an account: self sign-up in Auth0 or Cognito, any Google account when the client isn't limited to your Workspace domain, other organizations in a multi-tenant Entra ID app, and guest users. Limit sign-in at the provider (in Entra ID, set **Assignment required?** to *Yes*; in Okta, assign the app to groups; turn off self sign-up), or use [group rules](/docs/access/access-rules/) instead of `signed-in`.

## How it works

A static site can show a sign-in button and hide links in the browser, but its files are still there for anyone who asks: pages, OpenAPI specs, attachments and the search index can be downloaded with their URL. So a portal with `auth` is served by `rapidoc serve`, which checks the reader before it sends anything protected:

1. `rapidoc build` sorts the output by the rules: `dist/public/` (no protected content), `dist/protected/`, and `dist/rapidoc-server.json` with the rules.
2. `rapidoc serve dist` serves all three. On every request it reads the reader's session from an encrypted cookie, sends signed-out readers to your provider to sign in, and answers a reader the rules don't allow with "access denied". Search results are filtered per reader.

The contents of protected pages, specs and files never leave the server for a reader who may not see them. The public part stays plain static files, with cache headers so a CDN in front can hold the scripts, styles and fonts; `rapidoc serve` marks every protected answer as not cacheable.

What stays visible: the titles and paths of protected pages. Locked links keep their place in the header, sidebars and catalog, with a lock icon, so readers know there is more behind sign-in. Don't put anything confidential in a page title, a sidebar label or a URL.

> **Danger: Never upload all of dist/ to a static host**
> A static host serves every file it has, so `dist/protected/` would be readable by anyone. Run `rapidoc serve` on the whole `dist/`, or put only `dist/public/` on a static host or CDN.

The pages stay static. When a page loads, the header's sign-in button and the lock icons ask the server who the reader is.

`rapidoc serve` also hosts your APIs as tools for AI agents, at `/mcp` ([Model Context Protocol](/docs/tools/mcp-server/)). It is on unless you set `RAPIDOC_MCP=off`. An agent without a token sees only the tools of public APIs. A signed-in reader can copy a token for their agent from the user menu: with it, the agent sees the tools of the APIs that reader may see, and calls them as that reader. The token lasts as long as a sign-in (`session.maxAge`). To revoke all tokens, change `RAPIDOC_SESSION_SECRET`, which also signs everyone out.

## The `auth` key

| Key | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| `issuer` | The OpenID Connect issuer URL. `RAPIDOC_AUTH_ISSUER` overrides it. |
| `clientId` | The portal's client ID at the provider. `RAPIDOC_AUTH_CLIENT_ID` overrides it. |
| `scopes` | Scopes to request. Default `openid`, `profile`, `email`. |
| `claims.groups` | The claim with the reader's groups or roles, in the ID token or the provider's user info: a list, or names separated by spaces or commas. Default `groups`. Dotted paths work: `realm_access.roles`. |
| `session.maxAge` | How long a sign-in lasts: `30m`, `8h` (default), `7d`. |
| `logout` | `local` (default) signs out of the portal; `idp` also signs out at the provider, which then needs the portal URL as a post-logout redirect. |
| `label` | Text of the sign-in button. Default `Sign in`. |
| `audience` | The API the access token is for, sent as `audience` at sign-in (Auth0). `RAPIDOC_AUTH_AUDIENCE` overrides it. |
| `tryIt` | `true` gives **Try** the reader's access token. Default `false`. See [Try with the reader's token](/docs/access/try-it/). |

> **Caution: Secrets are never config keys**
> The session secret and the client secret are environment variables of `rapidoc serve`, because the config is committed to your repository and secrets must not be:
>
> - `RAPIDOC_SESSION_SECRET` (required): 32 characters or more, for example from `openssl rand -base64 32`. It encrypts the session cookie. Generate it once and keep it the same on every instance and across restarts; a new value signs everyone out.
> - `RAPIDOC_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`: only for a confidential client.
>
> Every variable: [Deploy with rapidoc serve](/docs/deploy/rapidoc-serve/#environment-variables).

## Words used in these pages

| Term | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| Identity provider | The service your company signs in with (Okta, Entra ID, Google...). The portal speaks OpenID Connect to it. |
| Issuer | The URL of the provider's sign-in service, for example `https://acme.okta.com/oauth2/default`. The portal reads the rest of the provider's settings from it. |
| Client ID, client secret | The portal's application at the provider, and its password. A *confidential client* has a secret; a *public client* has none and proves itself with PKCE alone. |
| Redirect URL | Where the provider sends the reader after sign-in: `<portal URL>/_rapidoc/auth/callback`. Some providers say redirect URI or callback URL. |
| Portal URL | `RAPIDOC_PUBLIC_URL`, else `site.url`, else the address the request came to. |
| ID token, access token | What the provider returns after sign-in. The ID token says who the reader is; the portal reads the name, email and groups from it, and from the provider's user info. The access token lets **Try** call your API ([Try with the reader's token](/docs/access/try-it/)). |
| Claim | One field of a token, such as `email` or `groups`. |
| Scopes | What the portal asks the provider for at sign-in: `openid profile email`, sometimes `groups`. |
| Tenant | Your organization's own space at a provider, with its own users (Entra ID, Auth0). |

## Next steps

- [Set up sign-in](/docs/access/setup/): register, configure, test locally and deploy.
- [Identity providers](/docs/access/providers/): the issuer, groups and audience for each provider.
- [Access rules](/docs/access/access-rules/): who may read which pages, APIs and files.
- [Deploy with rapidoc serve](/docs/deploy/rapidoc-serve/): containers, proxies and every environment variable.

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/access/overview/
