# Set up sign-in

> Step by step, for any OpenID Connect provider - register the portal, configure sign-in and access rules, test locally, and deploy.

This page takes a portal that already builds (`npx rapidoc build`) to one that signs readers in with your company's identity provider. The example uses Okta; the provider-specific values are in [Identity providers](/docs/access/providers/), and [SSO with Microsoft Entra ID](/docs/access/entra-id/) is the same walkthrough with every Entra ID screen.

Before you begin, you need:

- the address the portal will have, here `https://developers.acme.com`,
- permission to register applications at your identity provider,
- a host that can run a Node.js server for `rapidoc serve` ([Deploy with rapidoc serve](/docs/deploy/rapidoc-serve/)): a static host can't check who is reading.

## 1. Register the portal at your provider

Create an OpenID Connect application for the portal, of the **web application** kind (authorization code flow):

- **Redirect URLs** (also called sign-in redirect URIs or callback URLs):
  - `https://developers.acme.com/_rapidoc/auth/callback`
  - `http://localhost:8080/_rapidoc/auth/callback`, for testing on your computer
- **Post-logout redirect URLs**, only if you'll set `logout: idp`: `https://developers.acme.com/` and `http://localhost:8080/`.

Then note:

- the **issuer** URL, the address of your provider's sign-in service (Okta: `https://acme.okta.com/oauth2/default`),
- the **client ID** of the new application,
- its **client secret**, if the provider gave it one.

Most providers make a web application a *confidential client*: it has a client secret, which `rapidoc serve` keeps. If your provider offers a *public client* with PKCE only (a "single-page" or "native" app), that works too, with no secret to store. Either way the portal uses the authorization code flow with PKCE.

For access rules by group, make the provider put the reader's groups in the sign-in token: see [Groups](/docs/access/providers/#groups) for your provider.

## 2. Configure the portal

In `rapidoc.config.yaml`, add `auth` (who signs readers in) and `access` (who may read what):

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
site:
  url: https://developers.acme.com

auth:
  issuer: https://acme.okta.com/oauth2/default
  clientId: portal-web
  scopes: [openid, profile, email, groups]

access:
  default: public
  rules:
    - path: /docs/partners/**
      allow: signed-in
    - path: /apis/billing/**
      allow: { groups: [billing-team] }
```

Here everything is public except the partner guides (any signed-in reader) and the billing API (the `billing-team` group only). Use paths your portal has: a rule that matches no page fails the build. All keys: [The `auth` key](/docs/access/overview/#the-auth-key) and [Access rules](/docs/access/access-rules/).

The issuer and client ID are not secrets: they belong in the committed config. The client secret does not.

`rapidoc serve` comes from the package `@rapidoc/server`. A project made with `npm create rapidoc` already depends on it; otherwise add it: `npm install @rapidoc/server`.

## 3. Test on your computer

1. Put the secrets in a `.env` file in the project folder. Make sure `.gitignore` lists `.env` (the starter's does):

   ```bash title=".env"
   RAPIDOC_SESSION_SECRET=<output of: openssl rand -base64 32>
   # Only for a confidential client:
   RAPIDOC_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=<client secret>
   RAPIDOC_PUBLIC_URL=http://localhost:8080
   ```

   `RAPIDOC_SESSION_SECRET` encrypts the reader's session cookie. `RAPIDOC_PUBLIC_URL` is the portal's address, which the redirect URL is built from: here it overrides `site.url` (your production address).

2. Build, then serve with the `.env` file:

   ```bash
   npx rapidoc build
   node --env-file=.env node_modules/.bin/rapidoc serve dist
   ```

`rapidoc dev` doesn't do any of this: it shows every page, with no sign-in button. Sign-in and the rules work only with `rapidoc serve`.

## 4. Check that it works

Open `http://localhost:8080`:

| As | You should see |
| :--- | :--- |
| Signed out | Public pages open. Locked links show a lock icon. A partner guide sends you to Okta's sign-in, then back to that guide. |
| Signed in | Your name in the header and the partner guides. |
| Signed in, in `billing-team` | The billing API too. |
| Signed in, not in `billing-team` | An "access denied" page under `/apis/billing/`. |

If group rules never match, the server's log says so after each sign-in (`no "groups" claim for ...`): check [Groups](/docs/access/providers/#groups). For "redirect URI mismatch" errors, compare the provider's redirect URL with `RAPIDOC_PUBLIC_URL` + `/_rapidoc/auth/callback`, character for character.

## 5. Deploy

On the host, set the same environment variables in its secret or environment settings, with `RAPIDOC_PUBLIC_URL=https://developers.acme.com`:

- generate `RAPIDOC_SESSION_SECRET` once and keep it: the same on every instance and across restarts, or every reader is signed out,
- never put secrets in the repository or on the command line.

Then run `npx rapidoc build` and `npx rapidoc serve dist` there. Containers, several instances, proxies and every environment variable: [Deploy with rapidoc serve](/docs/deploy/rapidoc-serve/).

## Next steps

- [Access rules](/docs/access/access-rules/): rules by group or email, API versions, what is protected.
- [Try with the reader's token](/docs/access/try-it/): let **Try** call your API as the signed-in reader.
- [MCP server for agents](/docs/tools/mcp-server/): the same rules for AI agents.

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/access/setup/

---

# SSO with Microsoft Entra ID

> Step by step - put the portal behind Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) single sign-on, and give groups of employees access to their APIs with app roles.

This guide puts a portal behind your company's Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) sign-in: everyone in the company can read the portal, and only the billing team can read the billing API. Other providers work the same way; their differences are in [Identity providers](/docs/access/providers/).

It follows the same steps as [Set up sign-in](/docs/access/setup/), with every Entra ID screen. Before you begin, you need:

- a portal that builds (`npx rapidoc build`),
- the address it will have, here `https://developers.acme.com`,
- the right to register applications in your Entra tenant.

## 1. Register the portal in Entra ID

In the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com), open **Identity → Applications → App registrations** and choose **New registration**:

- **Name**: `Developer portal`.
- **Supported account types**: *Accounts in this organizational directory only*.
- **Redirect URI**: platform **Web**, URL `https://developers.acme.com/_rapidoc/auth/callback`.

For local testing, add `http://localhost:8080/_rapidoc/auth/callback` as a second redirect URI under **Authentication**.

From the app's **Overview**, note:

- **Application (client) ID**, for `auth.clientId`.
- **Directory (tenant) ID**, for the issuer: `https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant ID>/v2.0`.

Under **Certificates & secrets**, create a **client secret** and copy its **Value** (not its Secret ID).

> **Caution: Copy the secret now**
> Entra ID shows the secret's value only once. Store it in your secret manager right away; if it's lost, create a new one.

## 2. Create app roles for your groups

Entra ID's `groups` claim holds group IDs, not names, and is left out for users in more than 200 groups. App roles avoid both problems.

Under **App roles**, choose **Create app role**:

- **Display name**: `Billing team`
- **Allowed member types**: *Users/Groups*
- **Value**: `billing-team`. This is the name your access rules use.

Then open **Identity → Applications → Enterprise applications → Developer portal → Users and groups**, choose **Add user/group**, and assign the billing team's Entra group (or single users) to the **Billing team** role.

Optional: to let only the users and groups you assign sign in at all, set **Properties → Assignment required?** to *Yes* on the same enterprise application. Then assign everyone who should read the portal, not only the billing team.

## 3. Configure the portal

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
site:
  url: https://developers.acme.com

auth:
  issuer: https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant ID>/v2.0
  clientId: <application (client) ID>
  scopes: [openid, profile, email]
  claims:
    groups: roles # app roles arrive in the roles claim

access:
  default: signed-in # everyone the tenant lets sign in, guests included
  rules:
    - path: /apis/billing/**
      allow: { groups: [billing-team] }
    - path: /docs/billing/** # only if you have guides under docs/billing/
      allow: { groups: [billing-team] }
```

`signed-in` admits every account your tenant lets sign in to the app, including guest users. To limit the portal to people you choose, set **Assignment required?** to *Yes* (step 2) and assign them. A rule whose path matches no page fails the build, so keep only the rules for paths your portal has.

The issuer and client ID are not secrets, so they can live in the committed config. To use one build against a staging and a production tenant, set `RAPIDOC_AUTH_ISSUER` and `RAPIDOC_AUTH_CLIENT_ID` instead.

## 4. Build and run

Set three environment variables where the portal runs, from your secret manager or the host's environment settings, never in the repository or on the command line:

| Variable | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| `RAPIDOC_SESSION_SECRET` | Generate once with `openssl rand -base64 32` and keep it: the same on every instance and across restarts, or everyone is signed out. |
| `RAPIDOC_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` | The client secret's **Value** from step 1. |
| `RAPIDOC_PUBLIC_URL` | `https://developers.acme.com`, the address in the redirect URI. |

Then build and serve:

```bash
npx rapidoc build
npx rapidoc serve dist   # port 8080, or $PORT
```

To try it on your computer first, put the same variables in a `.env` file with `RAPIDOC_PUBLIC_URL=http://localhost:8080`, as in [Set up sign-in](/docs/access/setup/#3-test-on-your-computer).

## 5. Check that it works

| As | You should see |
| :--- | :--- |
| Signed out | The Microsoft sign-in page, then the page you asked for. |
| A user with the **Billing team** role | Every page, including the billing API under `/apis/billing/`. |
| A user without it | Every page except the billing API: an "access denied" page there. |

Role changes apply at the user's next sign-in.

To run it in a container or behind a load balancer, see [Deploy with rapidoc serve](/docs/deploy/rapidoc-serve/).

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Fix |
| :--- | :--- |
| `AADSTS50011`: the redirect URI does not match | The redirect URI in the app registration must equal `<RAPIDOC_PUBLIC_URL>/_rapidoc/auth/callback`, including `https` and any path the portal is served under. |
| `AADSTS7000215`: invalid client secret | Use the secret's **Value**, not its **Secret ID**, and check that it hasn't expired. |
| Signed in, but group rules deny access | Check that the user or their group is assigned to the app role, and that `auth.claims.groups` is `roles`. The server's log says when a sign-in carries no roles. Role changes apply at the next sign-in. |
| Email rules never match | Use app roles instead. Email rules need the optional claim `xms_edov` in the ID token (**Token configuration**), and match only users who have an email address in their Entra ID profile ([Access rules](/docs/access/access-rules/#who-may-read-allow)). |

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/access/entra-id/

---

# Identity providers

> The issuer URL, groups and Try audience for Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Auth0, Keycloak, Google, AWS Cognito, Ping, Authentik and Zitadel, and SAML-only providers.

Single sign-on works with any OpenID Connect provider. This page has what differs between them; the steps are the same everywhere ([Set up sign-in](/docs/access/setup/)). For every Entra ID screen, see [SSO with Microsoft Entra ID](/docs/access/entra-id/).

At every provider, register a web application with the authorization code flow, its redirect URL `<portal URL>/_rapidoc/auth/callback`, and with `logout: idp` the portal URL as a post-logout redirect. A confidential client (with a client secret) and a public client (PKCE only) both work; set `RAPIDOC_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` only for a confidential client.

## Issuer

`auth.issuer` is the provider's sign-in service. Copy it exactly: with or without the trailing slash, as the provider shows it.

| Provider | `issuer` |
| :--- | :--- |
| Okta | `https://<org>.okta.com/oauth2/default` (or another authorization server's URL) |
| Microsoft Entra ID | `https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant ID>/v2.0` |
| Auth0 | `https://<tenant>.<region>.auth0.com/`, with the slash |
| Keycloak | `https://<host>/realms/<realm>` |
| Google | `https://accounts.google.com` |
| AWS Cognito | `https://cognito-idp.<region>.amazonaws.com/<user pool ID>` |
| PingOne | `https://auth.pingone.<region>/<environment ID>/as` |
| Authentik | `https://<host>/application/o/<application slug>/` |
| Zitadel | `https://<instance>.zitadel.cloud`, or your own domain |

A wrong issuer stops `rapidoc serve` at start, with the address it couldn't reach.

## Groups

[Access rules](/docs/access/access-rules/) by group read the claim named in `auth.claims.groups` (default `groups`) from the ID token or the provider's user info. It must be a list of names, or names separated by spaces or commas. A dot in `auth.claims.groups` means a nested field (`realm_access.roles`), so a claim name can't contain one.

| Provider | Setting |
| :--- | :--- |
| Okta | On the authorization server, add a claim named `groups` to the ID token: **Security → API → Authorization Servers → default → Claims → Add Claim**, value type **Groups**, filter **Matches regex** `.*` (or a narrower one). If you include it only with the `groups` scope, add `groups` to `scopes`. |
| Microsoft Entra ID | Use app roles and `claims: { groups: roles }`. The `groups` claim holds group IDs, not names, and is left out for users in more than 200 groups. Steps: [SSO with Microsoft Entra ID](/docs/access/entra-id/#2-create-app-roles-for-your-groups). |
| Auth0 | Auth0 sends no roles by default. Add them in a Post Login Action, under a claim name with no dots, and set `claims: { groups: https://acme/roles }`. See below. |
| Keycloak | Realm roles: `claims: { groups: realm_access.roles }`. In **Client scopes → roles → Mappers → realm roles**, turn on **Add to ID token** or **Add to userinfo**. |
| Google | No groups. Use `emails` rules instead (`*@acme.com`); see [Google Workspace](#google-workspace). |
| AWS Cognito | User pool groups arrive as `cognito:groups`: `claims: { groups: "cognito:groups" }`. |
| Ping, Authentik, Zitadel | Add a claim with the reader's groups as a list of names, and set `auth.claims.groups` to its name. Zitadel's own roles claim is an object, which rules can't read: map it to a list in an Action. |

The Auth0 Action, under **Actions → Library → Create Action → Login / Post Login**, then added to the Login flow:

```js title="Add roles to the ID token"
exports.onExecutePostLogin = async (event, api) => {
  api.idToken.setCustomClaim("https://acme/roles", event.authorization?.roles ?? []);
};
```

After a sign-in that carries no groups, `rapidoc serve` logs `no "<claim>" claim for <user>: group rules can't match`. Group changes apply at the reader's next sign-in.

## Audience for Try

With [`tryIt`](/docs/access/try-it/), **Try** sends the reader's access token to your API, so the token has to be for your API:

| Provider | Setting |
| :--- | :--- |
| Okta | Use your API's authorization server as `issuer`. Its tokens are for that server's audience. |
| Microsoft Entra ID | Add your API's scope to `scopes`, for example `api://<API's application ID>/access_as_user`. |
| Auth0 | Set `audience` to the API's identifier. |
| Keycloak | Add an **Audience** mapper for your API's client to the portal's client. |
| Google | Not possible: Google's tokens are for Google's own APIs. |
| AWS Cognito | Add your resource server's scopes to `scopes`. |

## Google Workspace

Google's ID token has no groups, so rules can use `signed-in` or `emails`; Google marks addresses as verified. To keep other Google accounts out, set the OAuth consent screen's **User type** to **Internal**: then only accounts of your Workspace organization can sign in.

## SAML-only providers

Put an OpenID Connect broker in front: Keycloak, Authentik, Zitadel or Ory Polis. The portal signs in with the broker, which signs in with your SAML provider. Each broker's documentation has the steps.

## One build, several tenants

`RAPIDOC_AUTH_ISSUER`, `RAPIDOC_AUTH_CLIENT_ID` and `RAPIDOC_AUTH_AUDIENCE` override the config, so the same build can run against a staging and a production tenant.

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/access/providers/

---

# Access rules

> Decide who may read which pages, APIs and files - by sign-in, group or email.

The `access` key of `rapidoc.config.yaml` decides who may read which pages, API references, specs and files. It works together with [`auth`](/docs/access/overview/) and is enforced by `rapidoc serve`; `rapidoc dev` shows everything.

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
access:
  default: public
  rules:
    - path: /docs/partners/**
      allow: signed-in
    - path: /apis/billing/**
      allow: { groups: [billing-team] }
    - path: /docs/internal/**
      allow: { emails: ['*@acme.com'] }
```

| Key | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| `default` | Who may read what no rule matches: any `allow` value below. Default `public`. |
| `rules` | A list of `{ path, allow }`, checked top to bottom. |
| `rules[].path` | A URL path pattern, see below. |
| `rules[].allow` | Who may read what the path matches, see [Who may read](#who-may-read-allow). |

> **Caution: A rule must match something**
> A rule whose path matches no page or file **fails the build**, so a typo can't leave content public by accident. Write rules only for paths your portal has.

## Rules

Rules are checked top to bottom, and **the first rule whose path matches decides**. Put specific rules before general ones.

`path` is a URL path on the site, starting with `/`:

- `*` matches one path segment: `/docs/*/setup` matches `/docs/orders/setup`.
- `**` matches any number of segments, including none: `/docs/internal/**` matches `/docs/internal` and everything under it.

Guides in `docs/internal/` are at `/docs/internal/...`, so the folder and the path match ([Project structure](/docs/getting-started/project-structure/#docs)).

## Who may read: `allow`

| `allow` | Who may read |
| :--- | :--- |
| `public` | Everyone, signed in or not. |
| `signed-in` | Anyone who has signed in: everyone your provider lets sign in, which may be more than your staff ([who counts as signed in](/docs/access/overview/#choose-your-setup)). |
| `{ groups: [a, b] }` | Signed-in readers in at least one of these groups. |
| `{ emails: ['*@acme.com', 'jo@partner.io'] }` | Signed-in readers whose verified email matches one of these. `*` matches any characters. |

`groups` and `emails` can be combined in one `allow`: matching either one is enough (OR), not both.

Groups come from the claim named in `auth.claims.groups` (default `groups`); see [Groups](/docs/access/providers/#groups) for how each provider sends them.

An email counts only when the provider vouches for it in the token: `email_verified: true`, or on Microsoft Entra ID `xms_edov: true`. That one means the email's domain is verified by the reader's organization, not that the reader confirmed the address. Entra ID sends neither by default: add `xms_edov` as an optional claim, or better, use app roles ([SSO with Microsoft Entra ID](/docs/access/entra-id/)). `rapidoc serve` logs a hint when a reader's email can't match email rules.

## APIs and their specs

An API's reference page, its tag pages, its spec file and its embedded operations are all under `/apis/<id>`, where `<id>` is the API's `id` under `apis:` ([APIs](/docs/configuration/apis/)). One rule covers all of them:

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
access:
  rules:
    - path: /apis/billing/**
      allow: { groups: [finance] }
```

This covers every [version](/docs/api-reference/versions/) of the API too. To treat one version differently, put a rule for its URLs before the API's rule, since the first match decides:

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
access:
  rules:
    - path: /apis/billing/v4-beta/**
      allow: { groups: [finance-beta] }
    - path: /apis/billing/**
      allow: { groups: [finance] }
```

## What is protected

- Pages, specs, and the files of your project's `public/` folder.
- Search results: the search indexes are split per rule, so readers only find what they may read.
- The sitemap lists only public pages.

Not protected: the titles and paths of protected pages. Locked links stay visible in menus and the catalog with a lock icon, so readers know there is more behind sign-in; don't put anything confidential in a title or a URL.

Always public: the site's scripts, styles and fonts, the RapiDoc bundle, the logo and the favicon. Paths under `/_rapidoc/` belong to the portal: don't put pages or files there.

## What readers get

| Request | Allowed | Signed out | Signed in, not allowed |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Page | 200 | Sent to your provider's sign-in, then back to the page | 403 "access denied" page |
| Spec or other file | 200 | 401 | 403 |

## Build warnings

- A protected API whose spec is a URL: the build warns, because the spec stays public at that URL. Protect it where it is hosted.
- A public page that embeds an operation of a protected API: the build warns, because the operation won't load for readers who may not see the API.

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/access/access-rules/

---

# Try with the reader's token

> Let Try call your API with the signed-in reader's access token.

Every operation on an API reference page has a **Try** button, which sends the request to your API from the reader's browser. Without `tryIt`, readers fill in the **Authentication** panel of the reference page themselves: an API key, a token, or their own OAuth sign-in.

With `auth.tryIt`, a signed-in reader presses **Try** and the request carries their own access token, from their sign-in to the portal. Your API's own permission check answers, with that reader's permissions: `200` for a reader who may call it, `403` for one who may not. There is no token to copy and paste.

`tryIt` is optional. It needs:

- portal sign-in with `auth` ([Set up sign-in](/docs/access/setup/)),
- an API that accepts access tokens from the same provider, for the right audience ([below](#the-audience)),
- an API that allows the portal's address for cross-origin requests (CORS) with an `Authorization` header, as for any **Try** request.

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
auth:
  issuer: https://acme.okta.com/oauth2/default   # your API's authorization server
  clientId: portal-web
  tryIt: true
```

## How it works

1. At sign-in, `rapidoc serve` keeps the reader's access token in its own encrypted, `HttpOnly` cookie. The ID and refresh tokens are not kept at all.
2. Reference pages and embedded operations ask the server for the token, and fill it into the authentication panel for one security scheme of the spec:
   - the first `oauth2` or `openIdConnect` scheme,
   - else the first HTTP `bearer` scheme.
3. **Try** sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to the API.

The page keeps the token in memory only, never in local storage. It is handed only to pages of the portal itself (same origin), but every script running on those pages can fetch it, including analytics or other scripts you add with [`head`](/docs/configuration/site/#head-tags). Add only scripts you trust to a portal with `tryIt`.

The token expires on the provider's schedule, often after an hour, which can be well before the sign-in ends (`session.maxAge`). From then on, **Try** sends no token until the reader signs in again. A shorter `session.maxAge` keeps the two closer.

## The audience

The access token has to be for your API, not for the portal. Okta: use your API's authorization server as `issuer`. Auth0: set `audience` to the API's identifier. Microsoft Entra ID: add your API's scope to `scopes`, such as `api://<API's application ID>/access_as_user`. Every provider: [Audience for Try](/docs/access/providers/#audience-for-try).

## Before your API exists: the mock server

Point the spec's server at [`rapidoc mock`](/docs/tools/mock-server/), which checks each token's signature, audience and scopes the way your API would:

```yaml title="specs/billing.yaml"
servers:
  - url: http://localhost:4010/billing   # /<api id>
```

```bash
npx rapidoc mock --issuer https://acme.okta.com/oauth2/default --audience api://default
```

Signed-in readers then get `200` or `403` from the mock, depending on their own scopes. Okta's default authorization server issues tokens for the audience `api://default`.

## Troubleshooting

| What you see | Cause |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Try** has no token | The reader isn't signed in, `tryIt` isn't `true`, the token has expired, or the spec has no `oauth2`, `openIdConnect` or HTTP `bearer` scheme. |
| `401` from your API | The token is for another audience (see [The audience](#the-audience)), or it has expired. |
| A CORS error in the browser console, no response | Your API doesn't allow the portal's address, or the `Authorization` header, for cross-origin requests. |
| `403` from your API | The API's own check: the reader lacks the scope or permission. **Try** is working. |

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/access/try-it/

---

# Mock server

> Serve your specs with examples and generated data, validate requests, and check real OAuth scopes.

`rapidoc mock` serves every local spec of the portal on one port, each under `/<api id>` (a version other than the default under `/<api id>/<version>`). Readers can press **Try** before the API exists, and you can demo who may call what with real tokens.

```bash
npm install -D @rapidoc/mock
npx rapidoc mock
```

```text
http://localhost:4010/bookstore   → specs/bookstore.yaml
```

List the mock as a server in the spec, and the reference pages' **Try** calls it:

```yaml title="specs/bookstore.yaml"
servers:
  - url: http://localhost:4010/bookstore
    description: Local mock
```

This site's [example API](/apis/bookstore/) does exactly that: run `npm run mock:portal-site` in the [RapiDoc repository](https://github.com/rapi-doc/RapiDoc), where this site's source is, and **Try** answers. **Run workflow** on a [workflow](/docs/configuration/workflows/#run-against-the-mock) diagram uses the same server, so whole workflows run with no backend.

## What it answers

Examples from the spec first, else data generated from the schema; requests are validated against the spec; `Prefer` headers pick a documented response (`Prefer: code=404`); CORS is allowed for any origin. All of that, streamed responses (OpenAPI 3.2 `itemSchema`: Server-Sent Events and JSON Lines, sent one item at a time), and the options (`--port`, `--host`, `--seed`, `--stream-interval`), is on the [Mock Server](https://rapidocui.com/docs/mocking/mock-server/) page of the RapiDoc docs.

## Real token checks

Each operation's `security` is enforced. Start the mock with your OpenID Connect issuer, and bearer tokens must be signed by it, unexpired, for your audience and carry the operation's scopes (else `401` or `403`):

```bash
npx rapidoc mock --issuer https://acme.us.auth0.com/ --audience https://api.acme.com
```

`--issuer` and `--audience` can also come from `RAPIDOC_MOCK_ISSUER` and `RAPIDOC_MOCK_AUDIENCE`. Without `--issuer`, any bearer token passes and scopes aren't checked. Combined with [Try with the reader's token](/docs/access/try-it/), signed-in readers see `200` or `403` depending on their own permissions.

## Without a portal

The mock also works on plain spec files:

```bash
npx rapidoc mock ./specs                      # every OpenAPI file in the folder
npx rapidoc mock orders.yaml billing.json     # these files
```

Each spec is served under its file name: `orders-api.yaml` is `/orders-api`. The mapping is printed at start. This needs only `@rapidoc/cli` and `@rapidoc/mock`, not the portal.

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/tools/mock-server/

---

# MCP server for agents

> Every portal build carries its APIs and workflows as MCP tools; rapidoc serve hosts them at /mcp for AI agents, with the reader's own access.

AI agents can use your APIs the way readers do. `rapidoc build` turns every local spec and every workflow into [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) tool manifests, and `rapidoc serve` hosts them at `/mcp`: one endpoint for the whole portal, with the same access rules as the pages.

```text
dist/mcp/<api id>.json              the API's operations as tools, named <api id>_<operation>
dist/mcp/workflows/<id>.json        each workflow of the file as one tool, its inputs as the arguments
```

Nothing to configure: a build has the manifests whenever it has specs on disk (a spec that is a URL is left out).

## Connect an agent

With [`rapidoc serve`](/docs/deploy/rapidoc-serve/), the portal's MCP endpoint is `https://<your portal>/mcp` (Streamable HTTP).

An app that supports Streamable HTTP connects to that URL directly. In Cursor, add it to `.cursor/mcp.json`; in Claude Code, run one command:

```json title=".cursor/mcp.json"
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "acme-portal": { "url": "https://developers.acme.com/mcp" }
  }
}
```

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http acme-portal https://developers.acme.com/mcp
```

An app that speaks stdio only, such as Claude Desktop, connects through [mcp-remote](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-remote), a small program the app starts that forwards to the URL. This goes in Claude Desktop's own settings file:

```json title="claude_desktop_config.json"
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "acme-portal": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["mcp-remote", "https://developers.acme.com/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Other stdio-only apps take the same `mcpServers` entry in their own configuration file.

Without a token, the agent sees the public APIs and calls them without a reader's access token. A key set in the server's environment (see [Credentials of other kinds](#credentials-of-other-kinds)) is still sent, for every agent.

## Agents that sign in

On a portal with [sign-in](/docs/access/overview/), a signed-in reader opens the user menu and picks **Connect an AI agent**. **Get token** mints a token for their agents and shows the command that uses it:

```bash
npx mcp-remote https://developers.acme.com/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
```

With the token, the agent:

- sees the tools of every API the reader may see, and the workflows whose APIs they may all see;
- with [`auth.tryIt`](/docs/access/try-it/), calls the APIs with the reader's own access token, so the API's permission check applies to the agent as it does to **Try**.

The token is the reader's session (sealed like the cookies, never a copy of them) and lasts as long as the session. It opens exactly what the reader can see; a reader can't give an agent more than they have.

The reader's access token inside it is not refreshed. It usually expires sooner than the session; after that the agent still sees its tools, but its calls go out without that token and the API answers `401`. The reader then gets a new token from the menu.

## Credentials of other kinds

The reader's access token fills `oauth2`, `openIdConnect` and HTTP `bearer` schemes. For an API that takes an API key or HTTP Basic, set the credential in the environment of `rapidoc serve`, named like the exported project's: the scheme id in upper snake case (`PARTNER_KEY`), `<SCHEME>_USERNAME` and `<SCHEME>_PASSWORD` for Basic. For an API with one security scheme, `API_KEY` also works; an API with several needs a variable per scheme. Every agent then calls that API with the same key, with or without a token.

## From the command line

For an API that isn't in a portal, or to try its tools before building one, the CLI turns any spec into an MCP server:

```bash
npx rapidoc mcp export openapi.yaml --out-dir orders-mcp   # writes the server project
npx rapidoc mcp serve openapi.yaml                         # runs it over stdio, no files
```

`--base-url http://localhost:4010/orders` sends the calls to [`rapidoc mock`](/docs/tools/mock-server/), and `--arazzo flows.arazzo.yaml` adds the workflows as tools. The options, the credentials it reads and the agent configuration are on the [rapidoc mcp](https://rapidocui.com/docs/cli/mcp/) and [MCP Server](https://rapidocui.com/docs/ai/mcp-server/) pages of the RapiDoc docs.

## Exported servers

Readers can also download a standalone MCP server for one API from its reference page (**Export MCP server**, with `rapidoc.mcp: true`): a small stdio server with the same manifest and runtime, for agents that run where the portal can't be reached.

## Static hosting, and turning it off

The `/mcp` endpoint needs `rapidoc serve`: a static host only returns files, so a portal on GitHub Pages, Netlify or S3 has no endpoint. Agents can still use its APIs through [exported servers](#exported-servers) or [`rapidoc mcp serve`](#from-the-command-line), which run on the agent's machine.

To serve a portal with `rapidoc serve` but without the endpoint, set `RAPIDOC_MCP=off` in its environment: no `/mcp`, no agent tokens, and no "connect an AI agent" section in the user menu. `rapidoc serve` prints `MCP: off` when it starts.

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/tools/mcp-server/

---

# Validate

> Check your portal's OpenAPI specs and workflow files against the specification, locally and in CI.

```bash
npx rapidoc validate                       # every local spec in apis:, and the workflow files
npx rapidoc validate ./specs/orders.yaml   # one file
```

In a portal folder, `rapidoc validate` checks every local spec in `apis:` strictly against the OpenAPI Specification (required fields and types, path parameters, `$ref`s), with file, line and column for each error. It also warns about operations without an `operationId` (their page URLs change when their summary is edited), and checks that the steps of each workflow file resolve against your APIs.

What it checks, its output and its options (`--format json | sarif`, `--strict`, `--remote`) are described on the [rapidoc validate](https://rapidocui.com/docs/cli/validate/) page of the RapiDoc docs.

## In CI

It exits with code `1` when a spec has errors (or warnings, with `--strict`), so it can gate a pull request:

```yaml title=".github/workflows/docs.yml"
# in a job's steps:
- run: npm ci
- run: npx rapidoc validate
- run: npx rapidoc build
```

To see the problems on the pull request itself, upload a SARIF report to GitHub code scanning:

```yaml title=".github/workflows/docs.yml"
permissions:
  security-events: write
# in a job's steps:
- run: npx rapidoc validate --format sarif > rapidoc.sarif || true
- uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
  with:
    sarif_file: rapidoc.sarif
```

Projects created with `npm create rapidoc` have it as `npm run validate`.

Validating one file needs only `@rapidoc/cli`. Validating a whole portal also reads the config, so it needs `@rapidoc/portal`.

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/tools/validate/

---

# Lint

> Check what your portal's specs need to make good API pages, beyond being valid OpenAPI.

```bash
npx rapidoc lint                          # every API in rapidoc.config.*
npx rapidoc lint --strict --format sarif > rapidoc.sarif
```

A valid spec can still make a poor portal: operations without an `operationId` get page URLs that change when their summary is edited, bodies without examples leave **Try** and the mock server with nothing to show, tags that aren't declared have no description for their sidebar group. `rapidoc lint` finds those, after running [`validate`](/docs/tools/validate/)'s check.

The rules, their defaults, the output and the options are on the [rapidoc lint](https://rapidocui.com/docs/cli/lint/) page of the RapiDoc docs (`rapidoc lint --rules` prints them too).

## Settings

Set severities in `rapidoc.config.yaml`, for every API or per API. Most specific wins: `--rule` on the command line, then the API's entry under `lint.apis`, then `lint.rules`, then the defaults.

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
lint:
  rules:
    operation-description: warn
    no-unused-components: off
  apis:
    legacy: # an API that can't meet a rule yet
      operation-operationId: off
```

## In CI

Exit code `1` on errors (or warnings with `--strict`), `2` for a wrong rule name or severity:

```yaml title=".github/workflows/docs.yml"
# in a job's steps:
- run: npx rapidoc lint --strict
```

Upload a SARIF report to see the findings on the pull request, as the [Validate](/docs/tools/validate/#in-ci) page shows.

A portal folder needs `@rapidoc/portal`, to read the `apis:` list; one spec or a URL needs `@rapidoc/cli` alone.

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/tools/lint/

---

# Bundle

> Join a spec split over several files into one, for tools that can't follow $refs to other files.

```bash
npx rapidoc bundle --api orders -o dist/orders.yaml   # an API of rapidoc.config.*
npx rapidoc bundle specs/orders.yaml -o dist/orders.json
```

`rapidoc bundle` loads a spec and every file its `$ref`s reach, and writes one document: every `$ref` to another file becomes a component. The portal itself follows `$ref`s across files, so it doesn't need this; code generators, gateways and review tools often do.

`--api <id>` bundles the spec of an API in `rapidoc.config.*` (its default version) instead of a file, and needs `@rapidoc/portal`. What the bundle contains, how components are named, and the other options (`--dereference`, `--format`, `--no-validate`, `--remote`) are on the [rapidoc bundle](https://rapidocui.com/docs/cli/bundle/) page of the RapiDoc docs.

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/tools/bundle/

---

# Migrating

> Move a Zudoku or Redocly portal to RapiDoc Portal.

`rapidoc migrate` reads your existing portal's config and writes a `rapidoc.config.yaml` next to it.

```bash
npx @rapidoc/cli migrate                  # finds redocly.yaml or zudoku.config.* and asks to confirm
npx @rapidoc/cli migrate --from zudoku
npx @rapidoc/cli migrate --from redocly
```

Run it in the project folder. Use `npx @rapidoc/cli`, not `npx rapidoc`: before the CLI is installed, `npx rapidoc` looks for the npm package `rapidoc`, the `<rapi-doc>` web component, which has no command. Without `--from` it looks for a Redocly (`redocly.yaml`) or Zudoku (`zudoku.config.*`) config and asks before migrating it; in CI or a script, pass `--from` (or `--yes` to take the one found). An existing `rapidoc.config.yaml` is replaced, after asking in a terminal. It lists anything it could not convert; fix those before you build.

> **Caution:**
> It overwrites an existing `rapidoc.config.yaml`. Commit or copy yours first.

## From Zudoku

Reads `zudoku.config.ts`, `.mjs` or `.js`.

- Zudoku's top-level navigation items become the header tabs.
- The APIs become entries in `apis:`. APIs that had a custom path get a [redirect](/docs/configuration/docs-search-redirects/#redirects), because every reference page is `/apis/<id>`.
- An `input` list (one spec per version) becomes [`versions:`](/docs/api-reference/versions/), and each version's old URL gets a redirect. An input with `?prefix=`, which shows part of one file as a version, isn't supported: the query is dropped, so that version shows the whole file, and the migration warns about it.
- Imports from `zudoku/ui/...` and `<Stepper>` in MDX pages are rewritten at build time, so the pages work as they are.
- Zudoku's callout types (`info`, `warning`, `sparkles`, `rocket`, ...) render as before.
- `basePath` with `canonicalUrlOrigin` becomes the path of [`site.url`](/docs/configuration/site/#serving-under-a-path); a `basePath` without the origin gets a warning to set `site.url`. A `metadata.title` with `%s` becomes `site.titleTemplate`.

## From Redocly

Reads `redocly.yaml`, plus `sidebars.yaml` if it is there.

- The sidebars become a Documentation tab.
- The APIs become an API Catalog tab.
- `theme.openapi` becomes the theme and [`rapidoc:` attributes](/docs/api-reference/rapidoc-attributes/).
- `seo.siteUrl`, `seo.image` and `seo.projectTitle` become `site.url`, `site.image` and `site.titleTemplate`; `scripts.head` and `links` become [`head`](/docs/configuration/site/#head-tags) entries.

## After migrating

Install the CLI and the portal engine in the project, then check and preview the result:

```bash
npm install -D @rapidoc/cli @rapidoc/portal
npx rapidoc validate
npx rapidoc dev
```

Then check the header tabs and sidebars, and move remaining settings by hand with the [configuration reference](/docs/reference/config/).

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/tools/migrate/

---

# Static hosting

> Deploy the built portal to GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel, Cloudflare Pages or any web server.

Without `auth`, `rapidoc build` writes a plain static site to `dist/`. Host it anywhere that serves files.

```bash
npm run build                       # writes dist/
npx rapidoc build --out-dir site    # or another folder
```

Don't build into `public/`: that is the [folder of static files](/docs/getting-started/project-structure/#public) the build copies into the site.

Set `site.url` to the portal's public URL, for canonical links and the sitemap. To host the portal in a folder of another site, put the folder in the URL (`https://acme.com/developers`): links are built with `/developers` in front, and you upload `dist/` into that folder ([Serving under a path](/docs/configuration/site/#serving-under-a-path)).

## GitHub Pages

1. In the repository's **Settings → Pages**, set **Source** to **GitHub Actions**.
2. Set `site.url` to the address GitHub Pages gives the site:
   - a project repository is served under its name, so include it: `https://<user>.github.io/<repo>`;
   - a `<user>.github.io` repository, or a custom domain, is served at the root: `https://<user>.github.io`.
3. Commit a `package-lock.json` (`npm install` writes it): the workflow installs with `npm ci`, which needs it.
4. Add this workflow. Each push to `main` builds and deploys the portal; the run's summary shows its address.

```yaml title=".github/workflows/deploy.yml"
name: Deploy portal
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22 # the latest 22.x, at least 22.12
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx rapidoc validate
      - run: npx rapidoc build
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: dist
  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
    steps:
      - uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
```

`npx rapidoc validate` stops the deploy when a spec is invalid.

## Netlify, Vercel, Cloudflare Pages

| Setting | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| Build command | `npm run build` |
| Output folder | `dist` |
| Node.js version | 22.12 or later |

## Any web server

Copy `dist/` to the server's web root (Nginx, Apache, Caddy, S3 with CloudFront). Every page is a folder with an `index.html`, so the server needs no rewrite rules.

## Need sign-in (SSO)?

A static host can't check who is reading. There are two ways to put a portal behind your company's single sign-on.

If only calls to your API need a sign-in, and the documentation stays public, you need neither: readers sign in to your API from the API page itself, in the browser. See [OAuth 2 sign-in for Try](/docs/api-reference/reference-pages/#oauth-2-sign-in-for-try).

### The whole portal behind your SSO

When every signed-in employee may read everything, keep the plain static build and let the layer in front of it handle sign-in. No portal server runs:

- **Cloudflare Access** in front of Cloudflare Pages or any origin.
- **AWS**: an Application Load Balancer with OpenID Connect authentication in front of the files, or CloudFront with an authenticating edge function.
- **Your own server**: [oauth2-proxy](https://oauth2-proxy.github.io/oauth2-proxy/) in front of Nginx or Caddy.
- **Your host's own protection**, such as Vercel or Netlify on plans that offer SSO for deployments.

Leave `auth` and `access` out of the config: the portal doesn't know about the sign-in, so it shows no sign-in button or user menu, Try doesn't get the reader's token, and there is no MCP endpoint for agents.

### Some pages for some readers

For per-page and per-group rules, a sign-in button, Try with the reader's own token and MCP tools under the same rules, configure [`auth` and `access`](/docs/access/overview/) and deploy with [`rapidoc serve`](/docs/deploy/rapidoc-serve/). Public pages can still be cached by a CDN in front of it.

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/deploy/static-hosting/

---

# Deploy with rapidoc serve

> Run a portal with sign-in and access rules on Node or in Docker.

A portal with `auth` is served by `rapidoc serve` (`@rapidoc/server`). It serves the build, signs readers in through your provider, and enforces the [access rules](/docs/access/access-rules/) on every page, spec, file and search result.

```bash
npm install -D @rapidoc/cli @rapidoc/portal @rapidoc/server
npx rapidoc build
npx rapidoc serve dist   # port 8080, or $PORT
```

Set its [environment variables](#environment-variables) (`RAPIDOC_SESSION_SECRET`, `RAPIDOC_PUBLIC_URL`, and `RAPIDOC_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` for a confidential client) in the host's secret or environment settings, not on the command line, where they would end up in the shell history. To run it on your computer, see [Set up sign-in](/docs/access/setup/#3-test-on-your-computer).

- **Stateless**: the session is an encrypted cookie, so any number of instances can run behind a load balancer. No database.
- **Small**: it needs only Node, the CLI, `@rapidoc/server` and the build. Not `@rapidoc/portal`.
- **Agents too**: the APIs and workflows are MCP tools at `/mcp`, under the same rules. See [MCP server for agents](/docs/tools/mcp-server/).

You need it only for per-page or per-group access rules. A public portal, or one that is private as a whole behind your SSO proxy, is plain static files: see [Static hosting](/docs/deploy/static-hosting/#need-sign-in-sso).

## Availability and scaling

The server is a small Node process that reads the build from disk. It keeps nothing in memory between requests that another instance would need, so run it like any stateless web service:

- **Two or more instances** behind a load balancer, with the same `RAPIDOC_SESSION_SECRET`. Readers stay signed in whichever instance answers, and through restarts and deploys.
- **Health check**: `GET /_rapidoc/health` for the load balancer, Kubernetes or ECS.
- **Rolling deploys**: on `SIGTERM` the server stops taking new connections and exits, so the orchestrator can replace instances one at a time.
- **A CDN in front**: build assets (`_rapidoc/assets/`) are sent as `immutable` for a year and public pages revalidate, while anything that depends on the session is `private, no-store` and never cached.

A new release of the portal is a new build: build it in CI, ship `dist/` in the image, and roll the instances. There is no database to migrate.

## Environment variables

| Variable | Required | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `RAPIDOC_SESSION_SECRET` | with `auth` | Encrypts the session cookie. 32 or more characters, the same on every instance. Changing it signs everyone out. |
| `RAPIDOC_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` | confidential clients | Leave unset for a public client (PKCE only). |
| `RAPIDOC_PUBLIC_URL` | recommended | The portal's external URL: the redirect URL, and whether cookies are `Secure`. Default `site.url`, else the request's host. |
| `RAPIDOC_AUTH_ISSUER`, `RAPIDOC_AUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `RAPIDOC_AUTH_AUDIENCE` | no | Override `auth.issuer`, `auth.clientId`, `auth.audience`. |
| `RAPIDOC_MOUNT_PATH` | no | Path requests arrive under, when a proxy strips part of the portal's path. `--mount-path` wins. Default: the path of `site.url`. |
| `RAPIDOC_MCP` | no | `off` turns off the [MCP endpoint](/docs/tools/mcp-server/): no `/mcp`, no agent tokens, and no "connect an AI agent" section in the user menu. Default `on`. Any other value stops the server. |
| `PORT`, `HOST` | no | Default `8080` and `0.0.0.0`. `--port` and `--host` win. |
| `<SCHEME>`, `API_KEY` | no | API keys and HTTP Basic credentials for `/mcp` tool calls, named by the spec's security scheme id. See [MCP server for agents](/docs/tools/mcp-server/#credentials-of-other-kinds). |
| `EXTERNAL_HOSTS` | no | Hosts, comma-separated (`*` for any), that a workflow step's `x-operation` URL computed at run time may call from `/mcp`, besides the hosts the workflow names (its APIs' servers and URLs written out in its steps). |

The server refuses to start, with the reason, when a required value is missing or the provider can't be discovered.

## Behind a proxy that strips part of the path

A portal with `site.url: https://acme.com/sales/developers` is built and served under `/sales/developers`. When a gateway or ingress routes `/sales/*` to the server and strips `/sales`, requests arrive as `/developers/...`. Tell the server:

```bash
npx rapidoc serve dist --mount-path /developers
```

Links, redirects and the sign-in callback keep the full path the browser sees, `/sales/developers/...`. Without a proxy, the server answers under the path of `site.url` by itself.

## Docker

```dockerfile title="Dockerfile"
FROM node:22-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /portal
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npx rapidoc build

FROM node:22-alpine
WORKDIR /portal
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev && npm install --no-save @rapidoc/cli @rapidoc/server
COPY --from=build /portal/dist ./dist
ENV PORT=8080
EXPOSE 8080
CMD ["npx", "rapidoc", "serve", "dist"]
```

Health check for load balancers and Kubernetes: `GET /_rapidoc/health`.

## The build output

With `auth`, `rapidoc build` writes:

| Path | Holds |
| :--- | :--- |
| `dist/public/` | Everything anyone may read. Contains no protected content, so it can sit on a CDN. |
| `dist/protected/` | Pages and files behind a rule. |
| `dist/rapidoc-server.json` | The rules and zones the server enforces. |

Responses that depend on the session are `Cache-Control: private, no-store` with `Vary: Cookie`, so a CDN in front never caches a protected page for the wrong reader.

## Without `auth`

`rapidoc serve` also serves a plain static build, which is handy for a local check of the production build:

```bash
npx rapidoc build && npx rapidoc serve dist
```

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/deploy/rapidoc-serve/

---

# Render, DigitalOcean, Railway

> Deploy a portal to Render, DigitalOcean App Platform or Railway, in one click from the starter or from your own repository.

Render, DigitalOcean App Platform and Railway build the portal from your Git repository and run it with `rapidoc serve`. Every push rebuilds it. Sign-in works by adding environment variables, and agents get the `/mcp` endpoint.

## Try it in one click

The [starter repository](https://github.com/rapi-doc/rapidoc-portal-starter) deploys a sample portal as it is:

[![Deploy to Render](https://render.com/images/deploy-to-render-button.svg)](https://render.com/deploy?repo=https://github.com/rapi-doc/rapidoc-portal-starter)
[![Deploy to DO](https://www.deploytodo.com/do-btn-blue.svg)](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/apps/new?repo=https://github.com/rapi-doc/rapidoc-portal-starter/tree/main)
[![Deploy on Railway](https://railway.com/button.svg)](https://railway.com/deploy/eq5i1k?referralCode=tI_nkc)

To publish your own APIs, click **Use this template** on the starter's GitHub page, edit your copy, and deploy it as below.

## Your own repository

A portal made by `npm create rapidoc@latest` or `rapidoc init` is ready for all three. The hosts run the same scripts from `package.json`:

| Step | Command |
| :--- | :--- |
| Build | `npm run build` (`rapidoc build`) |
| Start | `npm start` (`rapidoc serve`, listening on `$PORT`, which the host sets) |
| Health check | `GET /_rapidoc/health` |
| Node.js | `engines.node` in `package.json` (22.12 or later) |

| Host | How |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Render** | Dashboard → New → Blueprint → your repository. It reads `render.yaml`. |
| **DigitalOcean App Platform** | Create App → GitHub → your repository. It detects the build and start scripts. Set the health check path to `/_rapidoc/health`. |
| **Railway** | New Project → Deploy from GitHub repo → your repository. It detects the build and start scripts. Set the health check path to `/_rapidoc/health`, and generate a domain under Networking. |

`@rapidoc/cli` and `@rapidoc/server` must be **dependencies**, not dev dependencies: DigitalOcean removes dev dependencies after the build, and `npm start` needs both. `@rapidoc/portal` is only needed for the build and stays a dev dependency. A portal made before this layout can be moved over with:

```bash
npm install @rapidoc/cli @rapidoc/server
npm pkg set scripts.start="rapidoc serve" engines.node=">=22.12.0"
```

and, for Render, this `render.yaml`:

```yaml title="render.yaml"
services:
  - type: web
    name: my-portal
    runtime: node
    plan: free
    buildCommand: npm install && npm run build
    startCommand: npm start
    healthCheckPath: /_rapidoc/health
```

## Sign-in

With [`auth`](/docs/access/overview/) in the config, set the secrets in the host's environment settings, never in the repository: `RAPIDOC_SESSION_SECRET` (32 or more random characters), `RAPIDOC_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` for a confidential client, and `RAPIDOC_PUBLIC_URL`, the portal's address, which must match the callback URL registered with your provider. All variables: [Deploy with rapidoc serve](/docs/deploy/rapidoc-serve/#environment-variables).

## Plans

- **Render**: a free web service sleeps after 15 minutes without visits, and the next visit waits up to a minute. A paid instance stays awake.
- **DigitalOcean**: web services run on paid instances; the starter's button uses the smallest one.
- **Railway**: billed by usage.

A portal without sign-in is also a plain static site, which these hosts (and others) serve for free without sleeping: see [Static hosting](/docs/deploy/static-hosting/).

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/deploy/cloud-platforms/

---

# CLI

> Every rapidoc command and option.

```bash
rapidoc <command> [options]
```

The command comes from the npm package `@rapidoc/cli`. In a project that has it installed, run it as `npx rapidoc <command>` or through the `npm run` scripts. Without it, run `npx @rapidoc/cli <command>`: `npx rapidoc` would look for the npm package `rapidoc`, the `<rapi-doc>` web component, which has no command.

| Command | Does |
| :--- | :--- |
| `init [dir]` | Scaffolds a portal in `dir` (default: the current folder), using the OpenAPI files already there. |
| `dev [dir]` | Starts the dev server with live reload on `http://localhost:4321`. |
| `build [dir]` | Builds the static portal into `dist/`. |
| `serve [dist]` | Serves a built portal, with sign-in and access rules. Default folder `dist`. |
| `preview <spec>` | Shows one spec (a file or URL) in `<rapi-doc>` on `http://localhost:4000`, reloading when a file in its folder changes. No portal needed. |
| `mock [dir \| spec...]` | Mock server for a portal's APIs, a folder of specs, or spec files (paths or URLs), each under `/<api id>`. |
| `validate [spec \| dir]` | Validates one spec (a file or URL), or every spec and workflow file in a portal ([Validate](/docs/tools/validate/), [every option](https://rapidocui.com/docs/cli/validate/)). |
| `lint [spec \| dir]` | Checks what a spec needs to make a good portal: operationIds, summaries, examples, security, declared tags ([Lint](/docs/tools/lint/), [every option](https://rapidocui.com/docs/cli/lint/)). |
| `bundle <spec>` | Writes a spec split over several files as one: other-file `$ref`s become components ([Bundle](/docs/tools/bundle/), [every option](https://rapidocui.com/docs/cli/bundle/)). |
| `pdf <spec>` | Writes the API reference of a spec as a PDF; `--api <id>` takes an API of the portal ([every option](https://rapidocui.com/docs/cli/pdf/)). Needs `rapipdf`. |
| `mcp export <spec>` | Writes an MCP server project for the spec ([MCP server](/docs/tools/mcp-server/#from-the-command-line), [every option](https://rapidocui.com/docs/cli/mcp/)). |
| `mcp serve <spec>` | Runs that MCP server over stdio, without writing files. |
| `migrate [--from <src>]` | Writes `rapidoc.config.yaml` from a `zudoku` or `redocly` project (found in the folder when `--from` is left out). |
| `doctor [dir]` | Checks Node, the packages' versions, the portal config and the browser bundle; `--format json` for bug reports. |
| `completion <zsh \| bash \| fish>` | Prints a completion script for the shell ([Shell completion](https://rapidocui.com/docs/cli/reference/#shell-completion)). |
| `help [command]` | Shows help, or one command's options and examples (same as `rapidoc <command> --help`). |
| `--version`, `-v` | Shows the version. |

Options and arguments can come in any order (`rapidoc build --out-dir public ./portal`). A misspelled command or option is an error with a suggestion (`Unknown option --outdir. Did you mean --out-dir?`).

## Options of the portal commands

| Option | Commands | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `--out-dir <path>` | build | Output folder. Default `dist`. |
| `--port <number>` | dev, serve, mock | dev: default `4321`; serve: `$PORT` or `8080`; mock: `4010`. |
| `--host <host>` | serve, mock | Address to listen on. Default `$HOST` (serve), else `0.0.0.0`. |
| `--open` | dev | Open the page in the browser. |
| `--mount-path <path>` | serve | Path requests arrive under, when a proxy strips part of the portal's path. Default `$RAPIDOC_MOUNT_PATH`, else the path of `site.url`. |
| `--issuer <url>`, `--audience <id>` | mock | OpenID Connect issuer and audience of accepted tokens ([Mock server](/docs/tools/mock-server/#real-token-checks)). |
| `--debug` | dev, build | Keep the temporary build workspace and print its path. |
| `--title <title>` | init | Site title. |
| `--spec <file>` | init | An OpenAPI file to include; repeat for more. Default: every one found in the folder. |
| `--starter-spec` | init | Use the starter spec instead of the OpenAPI files found. |
| `--force`, `-f` | init | Overwrite existing files (in a terminal, lists them and asks first). |
| `--no-install` | init | Skip `npm install`. |
| `--from <src>` | migrate | `zudoku` or `redocly` ([Migrating](/docs/tools/migrate/)). |
| `--format pretty \| json` | doctor | `json` for bug reports. |
| `--help`, `-h` | all | Show the command's help instead of running it. |
| `--quiet`, `-q` | all | Print errors and warnings only. |
| `--yes`, `-y` | all | Don't ask anything: take the default answer to every question. |

The options of `preview`, `validate`, `lint`, `bundle`, `pdf` and `mcp`, which work on any spec, are in the RapiDoc docs: [All Commands & Options](https://rapidocui.com/docs/cli/reference/).

## Questions

In a terminal, commands ask for what their options don't say, and `rapidoc` alone shows a menu of the common commands. When the output is piped, `CI` is set, or `--yes` is given, they never ask: they use the defaults, or stop and name the option to pass. Every question has an option, so any run can be scripted.

| Command | Asks | Option that answers it |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `init` | The site title, which of the OpenAPI files found to include, whether to run `npm install`. Then prints the command that does the same without questions. | `--title`, `--spec` / `--starter-spec`, `--no-install` |
| `init --force` | Whether to replace the existing files it lists. | `--yes` |
| `migrate` | Which project to migrate, when `--from` is left out (it looks for `redocly.yaml` and `zudoku.config.*`); whether to replace an existing `rapidoc.config.yaml`. | `--from`, `--yes` |
| `dev`, `serve`, `mock` | Whether to use the next free port when the port is taken. Without a terminal, `serve` and `mock` stop (`dev` moves to a free port by itself). | `--port`, `--yes` |

`Ctrl+C` on a question cancels the command (exit code `130`).

## Exit codes, packages and shell completion

`0` success, `1` a problem in the input (an invalid spec or config, a failed build, a missing package), `2` a wrong command line, `130` cancelled at a question. The CLI loads `@rapidoc/portal`, `@rapidoc/server` and `@rapidoc/mock` only for the commands that need them, and `rapidoc completion zsh|bash|fish` prints a completion script. Each is described in [All Commands & Options](https://rapidocui.com/docs/cli/reference/).

## Examples

```bash
rapidoc init my-portal --title "Acme Developer Portal"
rapidoc dev
rapidoc build ./my-api-portal
rapidoc serve dist --port 8080
rapidoc mock --issuer https://example.us.auth0.com/ --audience https://api.example.com
rapidoc mock ./specs --port 4011
rapidoc validate ./specs/orders-api.yaml
rapidoc lint --strict
rapidoc bundle ./specs/orders-api.yaml -o dist/orders-api.json
rapidoc migrate --from zudoku
```

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/reference/cli/

# Configuration keys

> Every key of rapidoc.config.yaml in one place.

Every key, with its default. The guides explain each section: [Configuration](/docs/configuration/overview/).

## `site`

| Key | Type | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `site.title` | string, **required** | |
| `site.description` | string | |
| `site.url` | URL | |
| `site.logo.src` | path, or `{ light, dark }` | |
| `site.logo.text` | string | the title when there is no image |
| `site.logo.alt` | string | |
| `site.logo.href` | URL | `/` |
| `site.favicon` | path | |
| `site.image` | path (needs `site.url`) or URL | |
| `site.titleTemplate` | string with `%s` | `'%s \| <title>'` |
| `site.noindex` | boolean | `false` |
| `site.banner.message` | string, required in a banner | |
| `site.banner.href` | URL | |
| `site.banner.dismissible` | boolean | `true` |
| `site.banner.background`, `site.banner.color` | CSS color | |

## `theme`

| Key | Type | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `theme.primary` | CSS color | `#f76b39` |
| `theme.mode` | `auto` \| `light` \| `dark` | `auto` |
| `theme.fonts.sans`, `theme.fonts.mono` | `{ family, url? }` | System fonts |
| `theme.css` | path, or list of paths | |

## `header`

| Key | Type | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `header.themeSwitcher` | boolean | `true` |
| `header.links[]` | `{ label, href \| items, icon?, style? }` | |
| `header.links[].style` | `link` \| `button` \| `primary` | `link` |
| `header.links[].items[]` | `{ label, href, icon?, description?, badge?, items? }` | |

## `navigation[]`

| Key | Type |
| :--- | :--- |
| `label` | string, required |
| `icon` | Phosphor icon name |
| `badge` | string, or `{ text, variant }` |
| exactly one of: `items`, `autogenerate`, `api`, `catalog: true`, `href` | the kind of tab |

Sidebar items: a page path string, or `{ label?, slug \| href \| items \| autogenerate \| api, version?, icon?, badge?, collapsed? }`.

A tab or sidebar item with `api` can have `version`: one of that API's versions.

## `apis[]`

| Key | Type | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `id` | lowercase letters, digits, dashes; **required** | |
| `spec` | path or URL; **required** unless `versions` is set | |
| `versions` | list of spec paths or `{ spec, version?, label? }`, instead of `spec` | the first is the default |
| `title` | string | `info.title` |
| `description` | string | `info.description` |
| `category` | string | `General` |

### `apis[].versions[]`

| Key | Type | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `spec` | path or URL, **required** | |
| `version` | lowercase letters, digits, dots, dashes; **required** for a URL spec | `info.version` |
| `label` | string | `info.version` |

## `workflows[]`

| Key | Type | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `file` | path to an Arazzo 1.x file; **required** | |
| `id` | lowercase letters, digits, dashes | the file name without `.arazzo.yaml` |
| `sources` | map of source description name → API id | sources named like an API id |

See [Workflows](/docs/configuration/workflows/).

## `docs`

| Key | Type | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `docs.dir` | path | `./docs` |
| `docs.toc` | `{ minHeadingLevel, maxHeadingLevel }` or `false` | levels 2 to 3 |
| `docs.editUrl` | URL | |

## `footer` (or `false`)

| Key | Type | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `footer.cta` | `{ title, description?, links? }`, up to 3 links | |
| `footer.newsletter` | `{ action, field?, title?, description?, button? }` | field `email`, button `Subscribe` |
| `footer.columns[]` | `{ title, links: [{ label, href }] }` | |
| `footer.social[]` | `{ icon: github \| x \| discord \| linkedin \| youtube, href }` | |
| `footer.copyright` | string | |
| `footer.branding` | boolean | `true` |

## Others

| Key | Type | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `rapidoc` | map of `<rapi-doc>` attributes | see [RapiDoc attributes](/docs/api-reference/rapidoc-attributes/) |
| `head[]` | `{ script }`, `{ link }` or `{ meta }`; `script` is attributes or inline code | |
| `search` | boolean | `true` |
| `llms` | `false`, or `{ description?, pageActions? }` | on; see [LLM output](/docs/configuration/llms/) |
| `llms.pageActions` | list of `copy`, `markdown`, `chatgpt`, `claude`, or `false` | all four |
| `redirects[]` | `{ from, to }` | |

## `auth`

| Key | Type | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `auth.provider` | `oidc` | `oidc` |
| `auth.issuer` | URL | `$RAPIDOC_AUTH_ISSUER` |
| `auth.clientId` | string | `$RAPIDOC_AUTH_CLIENT_ID` |
| `auth.scopes` | string list | `openid, profile, email` |
| `auth.claims.groups` | claim name or dotted path | `groups` |
| `auth.session.maxAge` | `30m`, `8h`, `7d` | `8h` |
| `auth.logout` | `local` \| `idp` | `local` |
| `auth.label` | string | `Sign in` |
| `auth.audience` | string | `$RAPIDOC_AUTH_AUDIENCE` |
| `auth.tryIt` | boolean | `false` |

## `access`

| Key | Type | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `access.default` | allow | `public` |
| `access.rules[]` | `{ path, allow }`, first match wins | |

An allow is `public`, `signed-in`, or `{ groups?, emails? }`.

## `lint`

Settings for [`rapidoc lint`](/docs/tools/lint/); the build ignores them.

| Key | Type | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `lint.rules` | `{ <rule>: error \| warn \| off }` | each rule's own default |
| `lint.apis` | `{ <api id>: { <rule>: severity } }`, wins over `rules` | |

## JSON Schema

The full schema ships as `@rapidoc/portal/schema.json`. Point your editor at it for autocomplete:

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
# yaml-language-server: $schema=./node_modules/@rapidoc/portal/schema.json
```

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/reference/config/

# Programmatic API

> Build, serve and mock portals from your own Node.js scripts.

Every CLI command is a function you can call from Node.js 22.12 or later. All packages are ES modules.

## `@rapidoc/portal`

```js title="build.mjs"
import { buildPortal, startDevServer, loadConfig } from '@rapidoc/portal';

const result = await buildPortal('./my-portal', { outDir: 'dist' });
// { success, apisCount, outDir, durationMs, access? }

const server = await startDevServer('./my-portal', { port: 4321 });
await server.stop(); // stops the server and removes its workspace

const { config } = await loadConfig('./my-portal'); // the normalized config
```

With sign-in, `result.access` is `{ protectedPages, protectedFiles, zones, warnings }`.

Both `buildPortal` and `startDevServer` take `keepWorkspace: true` (the CLI's `--debug`) to keep the generated site in `.rapidoc-temp/`.

Other exports:

| Export | Does |
| :--- | :--- |
| `normalizeConfig`, `migrateConfig`, `RapidocConfigSchema` | Config helpers and the zod schema. |
| `compileMarkdoc`, `markdocTags` | Render Markdoc with the portal's tags to HTML. |
| `buildSearchIndex`, `searchRecords` | The search index of guides and operations. |
| `checkPortalSpecs`, `checkApiSpec` | What `rapidoc validate` runs. |

Subpath exports: `@rapidoc/portal/config`, `/markdoc`, `/search`, `/components` (MDX components) and `/schema.json`.

## `@rapidoc/server`

```js title="serve.mjs"
import { createApp, startServer } from '@rapidoc/server';

const { app } = await createApp({ distDir: 'dist' }); // a Hono app: mount it or add middleware
const server = await startServer({ distDir: 'dist', port: 8080 });
await server.close();
```

## `@rapidoc/mock`

```js title="mock.mjs"
import { createMockApp, startMockServer } from '@rapidoc/mock';

const { app } = await createMockApp({
  apis: [{ id: 'orders', fullPath: '/abs/path/orders.yaml' }],
  issuer: 'https://example.us.auth0.com/',
  audience: 'https://api.example.com',
});
// app.fetch(request), or mount it in your own server

const mock = await startMockServer({ apis, port: 4010 });
// { url, port, apis, skipped, close }
```

## `create-rapidoc`

```js title="scaffold.mjs"
import { scaffoldProject, findOpenApiSpecs } from 'create-rapidoc/scaffold';

const specs = findOpenApiSpecs('./my-portal');
scaffoldProject('./my-portal', { title: 'Acme Developers', specs });
```

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/reference/programmatic-api/

---

# How a build works

> What rapidoc dev and rapidoc build do, step by step.

You don't need this page to write or deploy a portal. It explains what the commands do behind the scenes, for debugging a build or a leftover folder.

`rapidoc build` runs five steps:

1. **Load and validate** `rapidoc.config.yaml`. An unknown key or a wrong value stops the build with its path.
2. **Create a temporary workspace** at `<project>/.rapidoc-temp/<dev|build>-<pid>-<n>/`, one per run, so a build never disturbs a running `rapidoc dev`. It holds a normalized copy of `docs/`, the `public/` folder, the specs, the RapiDoc bundle and the search index.
3. **Render the site** from the workspace with [Astro](https://astro.build/) and its documentation theme, Starlight. The pages (home, guides, catalog, API reference) and their components come from `@rapidoc/portal`.
4. **Write the static site** to `dist/` (or `--out-dir`). With sign-in configured, the output is then split into `public/`, `protected/` and `rapidoc-server.json` for `rapidoc serve`.
5. **Delete the workspace**, even when the build fails. Your project ends up exactly as it was, plus `dist/`.

`rapidoc dev` runs steps 1 to 3 and serves the site on `http://localhost:4321`. It watches the project: guide edits appear immediately, and a change to the config or a spec restarts the server. Its workspace is removed when the server stops, including with Ctrl+C.

> **Note: A leftover .rapidoc-temp folder**
> A run killed before it can clean up (`kill -9`, a crash) leaves its folder behind. The next run removes the folders of processes that are no longer running.

## Why not the OS temp folder?

Astro only compiles pages that share a parent folder with the site root, so the workspace has to live inside your project.

## Debugging the engine

```bash
npx rapidoc build --debug
```

`--debug` keeps the workspace and prints its path, so you can inspect the generated site.

Source: https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/reference/how-it-works/
